paper_title: New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth
context_brief: Analogue of the three-valued theorem for four-valued exponents
original_question: Suppose x -> x^s is a power permutation of a finite field L, and call s four-valued when the reduced spectrum of the corresponding Weil sums W_{L,s}(a) on a in L^× has exactly four distinct values. Katz proved that in the three-valued case the exponent must be singular, must satisfy s ≡ 1 (mod p - 1), and has integral spectrum {0, A, B}. Find an analogue of that theorem for four-valued exponents: determine what structural restrictions on s and on the spectrum must hold when the reduced spectrum has exactly four values.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime, $L = \mathbb{F}_q$ with $q = p^n$, and let $\psi\colon L \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ be the canonical additive character $\psi(x) = \exp(2\pi i\,\mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p)$. For an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s,q-1)=1$ (so that $x \mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $L$), define the Weil sum
$$W_{L,s}(a) \;=\; \sum_{x \in L} \psi(x^s - a x), \qquad a \in L.$$
The reduced spectrum of $W_{L,s}$ is the set $\{\,W_{L,s}(a) : a \in L^\times\,\}$ of distinct values taken on the nonzero elements. Call $s$ $k$-valued (over $L$) when this reduced spectrum has exactly $k$ elements. An exponent $s$ is called singular if $s \equiv p^j \pmod{q-1}$ for some $j$ would fail (precise standard definition: $s$ is degenerate/non-singular if $s$ is a power of $p$ modulo $q-1$; otherwise non-degenerate; "singular" is taken in the sense used for three-valued spectra).

It is known (three-valued theorem) that if $s$ is three-valued then $s$ is singular, $s \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$, and the reduced spectrum $\{0, A, B\}$ consists of rational integers.

Problem: Establish an analogous structural theorem for four-valued exponents. Specifically, determine which congruence conditions on $s$ (modulo $p-1$ or otherwise), which singularity/non-degeneracy conditions, and which arithmetic restrictions on the four values of the reduced spectrum (e.g. integrality or rationality) must hold whenever $s$ is four-valued over $L$.
status_search_result: Katz and Wong (2023/2024) established a rationality result for four-valued Weil spectra: if the spectrum has exactly four values, then all four are rational integers, with the sole exception of $L=\mathbb{F}_5$ and $s \equiv 3 \pmod 4$. This addresses the integrality aspect of the analogue, but the full structural analogue (congruence on $s$ modulo $p-1$ and singularity in the same form as the three-valued theorem) is not fully resolved.

paper_title: New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth
original_question: Let F(x) = mu(x^s) for an exponent s on a finite field L of order q, and let A_1, ..., A_n be the distinct nonzero values occurring in the spectrum of F. Determine for which exponents s the product of the nonzero spectral values A_1 A_2 ... A_n is divisible by q.
self_contained_problem:
Let $L = \mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field of order $q$, where $q$ is a prime power, and let $\mu \colon L \to \mathbb{C}$ be the canonical additive character of $L$ (i.e., $\mu(x) = e^{2\pi i \,\mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p}$, where $p$ is the characteristic of $L$). For an integer $s$ with $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$ (so that $x \mapsto x^s$ is a permutation of $L$), define the Weil sum
$$W_s(a) = \sum_{x \in L} \mu(a x^s + x), \qquad a \in L^*.$$
The (nonzero) spectrum of the function $F(x) = \mu(x^s)$ is the multiset of distinct nonzero values $A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n$ taken by $W_s$ as $a$ ranges over $L^*$. 

Determine all exponents $s$ for which the product
$$\prod_{i=1}^n A_i$$
of the distinct nonzero spectral values is divisible by $q$ (as an algebraic integer in the appropriate cyclotomic ring).

No solution appears in the available sources.

context_brief: Classification of nice exponents over prime fields
original_question: Fix a finite field L and an invertible exponent s. For u, v in L, define N(u,v) to be the number of pairs (x,y) in L^2 satisfying x + y = u and x^s + y^s = v. Call s nice when, as v ranges over L with v ≠ 1, the values N(1,v) take at most three distinct values. Numerical experiments over prime fields of characteristic p < 5000 found that every nice exponent s not equivalent to 1 under the relation generated by Frobenius twists s′ ≡ p^j s (mod q - 1) and inversion seems to come from the paradigmatic families described earlier in the paper. Must this always happen for every nice exponent over every prime field?

$$N(u,v) = \#\{(x,y)\in L\times L : x+y=u,\ x^s+y^s=v\}.$$
Call $s$ "nice" if, as $v$ ranges over $L\setminus\{1\}$, the multiset $\{N(1,v)\}$ takes at most three distinct values.

Declare two exponents $s, s'$ equivalent (write $s\approx s'$) if $s'\equiv p^j s \pmod{p-1}$ for some integer $j\ge 0$ (a Frobenius twist; trivial in the prime-field case) or $s s' \equiv 1 \pmod{p-1}$ (inversion), and take the equivalence relation generated by these.

original_question: Let s be an invertible exponent over a finite field of odd characteristic, with s not equivalent to 1 under the equivalence generated by Frobenius twists and inversion. For v in the field, let N(1,v) count pairs (x,y) in L^2 satisfying x + y = 1 and x^s + y^s = v. Must there always exist some v for which N(1,v) = 2? In other words, is 2 always a differential multiplicity for every such invertible exponent?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L = \mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of odd characteristic $p$, with $q = p^n$. An exponent over $L$ is an integer $s$ considered modulo $q-1$; it is called invertible if $\gcd(s, q-1) = 1$. Two exponents $s, t$ are equivalent (written $s \approx t$) under the equivalence relation generated by the Frobenius twist $s \mapsto p s \pmod{q-1}$ and, when applicable, multiplicative inversion $s \mapsto s^{-1} \pmod{q-1}$. For an exponent $s$ and an element $v \in L$, define
$$N(1,v) = \#\{(x,y) \in L^2 : x + y = 1 \text{ and } x^s + y^s = v\}.$$
A value $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ is called a differential multiplicity of $s$ if there exists some $v \in L$ such that $N(1,v) = m$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite field $L$ of odd characteristic and every invertible exponent $s$ over $L$ with $s \not\approx 1$, the value $2$ is a differential multiplicity of $s$; equivalently, there exists $v \in L$ with $N(1,v) = 2$.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Give a mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics by providing an axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems suitable for the foundations of statistical physics, and by developing a rigorous theory of the limiting processes that lead from an atomistic description to the laws of motion of continua.
self_contained_problem:
Hilbert's sixth problem: Provide a complete mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics. Specifically, accomplish the following two tasks.

(i) Develop an axiomatic foundation of probability theory together with the corresponding limit theorems (laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, ergodic theorems, etc.) in a form suitable to serve as a rigorous foundation for statistical physics, including classical statistical mechanics and its extensions.

(ii) Develop a rigorous mathematical theory of the limiting processes that lead from an atomistic (microscopic) description of matter — for example, a system of N interacting classical particles evolving according to Newton's equations of motion — to the macroscopic laws of motion of continua, such as the compressible Euler equations, the incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations, and other equations of continuum mechanics. This is to be carried out through the appropriate scaling limits (e.g., the Boltzmann–Grad limit producing kinetic equations of Boltzmann type, followed by hydrodynamic limits producing fluid equations), with full mathematical rigor and under physically meaningful hypotheses on the underlying particle dynamics.
category_tag: Axiomatization of physics and hydrodynamic limits
status_search_result: Part (i) on the axiomatic foundation of probability is widely regarded as solved by Kolmogorov's 1933 measure-theoretic axiomatization together with the classical limit theorems. Part (ii) on the rigorous derivation of continuum equations from atomistic dynamics has seen major progress, including the recent 2025 work of Deng, Hani, and Ma deriving the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier–Stokes–Fourier equations from hard-sphere Newtonian dynamics via the Boltzmann equation, though this work has drawn critical commentary regarding its physical scope (dilute-gas regime, molecular chaos assumption) and the full program of axiomatizing physics remains incomplete.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine whether P equals NP, meaning whether every problem whose proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time also has an algorithm that can find a solution in polynomial time.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\{0,1\}^*$ denote the set of all finite binary strings. A language is a subset $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$. A deterministic Turing machine $M$ is said to decide $L$ in polynomial time if there exists a polynomial $p$ such that, for every input $x \in \{0,1\}^*$, $M$ halts after at most $p(|x|)$ steps and accepts if and only if $x \in L$. The class $\mathbf{P}$ is the set of all languages decidable by some deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.

The class $\mathbf{NP}$ is the set of all languages $L$ for which there exist a polynomial $q$ and a language $V \in \mathbf{P}$ such that
$$L = \{ x \in \{0,1\}^* : \exists\, y \in \{0,1\}^* 	ext{ with } |y| \le q(|x|) 	ext{ and } (x,y) \in V \}.$$
Intuitively, $\mathbf{NP}$ consists of those decision problems whose "yes"-instances admit a certificate verifiable in polynomial time.

Question: Is $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{NP}$? Either prove that every language in $\mathbf{NP}$ belongs to $\mathbf{P}$, or exhibit a language in $\mathbf{NP}$ that provably does not belong to $\mathbf{P}$.
status_search_result: The P versus NP problem is universally regarded as open. It is listed as one of the Clay Mathematics Institute's Millennium Prize Problems, and no proof in either direction has been accepted by the mathematical community as of 2026.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Extend the mathematical model of general equilibrium theory so that it includes price-adjustment dynamics rather than only equilibrium states.
self_contained_problem:
In the classical Arrow–Debreu model of general equilibrium, an exchange economy consists of finitely many agents trading finitely many commodities, where each agent has preferences and an initial endowment; this gives rise to an aggregate excess demand function $Z : \mathbb{R}^{\ell}_{++} \to \mathbb{R}^{\ell}$ on the strictly positive price orthant satisfying Walras' law $p \cdot Z(p) = 0$ and homogeneity of degree zero. A price vector $p^*$ is an equilibrium if $Z(p^*) \le 0$. The standard theory establishes existence (and, generically, finiteness) of such equilibria but treats only the static equilibrium notion.

Problem: Develop a mathematical extension of the general equilibrium model that incorporates an explicit price-adjustment dynamics—i.e., a well-posed dynamical system on the price space (such as a flow or differential inclusion driven by excess demand, or a more general learning/tâtonnement-type process)—with the following properties:

(i) Equilibria of the static general equilibrium model are equilibria (rest points) of the dynamics.

(ii) The dynamics is defined and economically meaningful for a generic class of excess demand functions (i.e., not requiring gross substitutability, the weak axiom of revealed preference, or other restrictive assumptions known to be sufficient for convergence of classical tâtonnement).

(iii) For (almost) every excess demand function in this generic class, trajectories of the dynamics converge to an equilibrium price vector from (almost) every initial price.

Provide such a model, together with a proof of global (generic) convergence, or otherwise establish obstructions to its existence.
status_search_result: Smale himself proposed and studied global Newton-type price adjustment processes (e.g., "A Convergent Process of Price Adjustment and Global Newton Methods"), and various tâtonnement, learning, and dynamic-programming approaches have been investigated since. However, no fully satisfactory dynamic extension of general equilibrium theory yielding generic global convergence has been established, and the problem is generally regarded as still open in the form stated by Smale.

original_question: For Newtonian gravitating particles, prove that the set of initial conditions that fail to produce global solutions has measure zero, and determine whether non-collisional singularities can occur in the Newtonian N-body problem.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Newtonian N-body problem: N point particles with masses m_1,...,m_N > 0 in R^3 evolve according to
  m_i x_i''(t) = sum_{j != i} G m_i m_j (x_j - x_i)/|x_j - x_i|^3,
with initial positions x_i(0) ∈ R^3 (mutually distinct) and initial velocities v_i(0) ∈ R^3. A singularity at time T < ∞ is a maximal solution that cannot be continued past T. It is called a collision singularity if the limit positions exist with at least two coinciding, and a non-collision singularity otherwise (equivalently, some particle escapes to spatial infinity in finite time or oscillates without limit).

Solve both of the following:

(A) Prove that the set of initial conditions (x_1(0),...,x_N(0), v_1(0),...,v_N(0)) in the phase space (for which the configuration is non-collisional) that fail to yield a global-in-time solution has Lebesgue measure zero.

(B) Determine for which N ≥ 2 there exist non-collision singularities in the Newtonian N-body problem.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Develop a comprehensive theory of the long-time behavior of dynamical systems that also includes a theory for the onset of turbulence and for fully developed turbulence.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a comprehensive mathematical theory describing the long-time (asymptotic) behavior of dynamical systems — including finite-dimensional flows and infinite-dimensional systems arising from partial differential equations such as the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on a bounded domain or torus in three dimensions. The desired theory should:

1. Provide rigorous tools to classify and characterize attractors, invariant measures, and statistical limits for general nonlinear dissipative dynamical systems as time tends to infinity.

2. Yield a rigorous mathematical theory of the onset of turbulence: identify and analyze the sequence of bifurcations and transitions (e.g., loss of stability of laminar solutions, emergence of complex/chaotic regimes) by which solutions of the Navier–Stokes equations (or comparable model systems) pass from regular flow to turbulent flow as a control parameter such as the Reynolds number increases.

3. Yield a rigorous mathematical theory of fully developed turbulence: derive from first principles the statistical laws of high-Reynolds-number turbulent flows, including, for instance, the existence of a universal inertial-range energy spectrum, Kolmogorov-type scaling laws, anomalous dissipation, intermittency, and the structure of invariant measures supported on turbulent regimes.

Produce such a unified theory, or prove rigorous theorems establishing its principal components.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Resolve the open ergodic-theory questions identified by Simon: determine ergodicity of gases with soft cores, explain approach to equilibrium, and establish asymptotic abelianness for quantum Heisenberg dynamics.
self_contained_problem:
Resolve the following three problems in ergodic theory of statistical mechanics:

(A) Ergodicity of gases with soft cores. Consider a classical system of N point particles in a box (or in ℝ^d) interacting via a smooth pair potential V: ℝ^d → ℝ that is finite at the origin (a "soft core"), with Hamiltonian H(q,p) = Σ_i |p_i|²/(2m) + Σ_{i<j} V(q_i − q_j). Show that the Hamiltonian flow on a constant-energy surface is ergodic with respect to the microcanonical (Liouville) measure for generic such V (and, in particular, for natural classes of soft-core potentials).

(B) Approach to equilibrium. For a suitable infinite-volume dynamical system of classical or quantum statistical mechanics (e.g. an infinite ideal or interacting gas, or a quantum lattice/continuous system), starting from a non-equilibrium initial state μ_0, prove that the time-evolved state μ_t converges, as t → ∞, to an equilibrium (Gibbs) state in an appropriate topology, and give a rigorous derivation of irreversible macroscopic behavior from the underlying reversible microscopic dynamics.

(C) Asymptotic abelianness for quantum Heisenberg dynamics. Let A be the quasi-local C*-algebra of the quantum Heisenberg model on Z^d (d ≥ 2) built from spin-s operators at each site, with formal Hamiltonian H = −Σ_{⟨x,y⟩} J S_x · S_y, and let α_t denote the corresponding time evolution on A. Prove that the dynamics is asymptotically abelian in the sense that, for every pair A, B ∈ A of strictly local observables,
   lim_{t → ∞} ‖[α_t(A), B]‖ = 0,
or, in a weaker formulation, that this commutator tends to zero in some natural (e.g. weak, mean ergodic, or state-dependent) sense.
status_search_result: These three problems form Barry Simon's problem BS2 from his lists of open problems in mathematical physics. No general resolution is reported: ergodicity for soft-core interacting gases remains unknown, a fully rigorous derivation of approach to equilibrium from Hamiltonian/quantum dynamics is a long-standing open problem, and asymptotic abelianness for the quantum Heisenberg dynamics is established only in restricted settings (e.g. strong asymptotic abelianness is known for certain entropic K-systems, but not for Heisenberg dynamics in general).

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Put quantum field theory on a rigorous mathematical footing by constructing quantum chromodynamics, building a nontrivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theory, proving that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory, or proving that no nontrivial lattice cutoff theory exists.
self_contained_problem:
Place quantum field theory on a rigorous mathematical footing by achieving at least one of the following four goals.

(A) Construction of QCD. Give a precise mathematical construction of quantum chromodynamics, the non-abelian gauge theory with gauge group SU(3) coupled to quark fields, on four-dimensional Minkowski (or Euclidean) space-time. The construction must produce a quantum field theory satisfying a suitable set of axioms (e.g. the Wightman or Osterwalder–Schrader axioms, suitably adapted to gauge theories), with the expected particle content and symmetries.

(B) Renormalizable but not super-renormalizable QFT. Construct any nontrivial quantum field theory in some space-time dimension that is renormalizable but not super-renormalizable, in the sense that the theory's interaction is dimensionless (marginal) rather than having positive mass dimension. The constructed theory must be nontrivial (i.e., not a (generalized) free field) and must satisfy a precise set of axioms for a relativistic quantum field theory.

(C) Inconsistency of QED. Prove that quantum electrodynamics—the U(1) gauge theory coupled to a Dirac spinor field in four-dimensional space-time—cannot be realized as a nontrivial mathematically consistent quantum field theory satisfying the Wightman (or equivalent) axioms.

(D) Nonexistence of nontrivial lattice continuum limit. Prove that no nontrivial continuum limit exists for a lattice-regularized quantum field theory in the relevant case (for example, a φ⁴ theory in four space-time dimensions): that is, prove that every sequence of lattice cutoff theories whose lattice spacing tends to zero, with parameters tuned to approach a critical point, converges only to a (generalized) free field.

Provide a complete mathematical proof for at least one of (A), (B), (C), or (D).
status_search_result: All four sub-problems remain open. Constructive QFT has not yet produced a rigorous construction of QCD or any nontrivial strictly renormalizable (not super-renormalizable) 4D theory; recent results (e.g., Aizenman–Duminil-Copin 2021) prove triviality of φ⁴ in four dimensions, which is progress toward (D) for that specific model but does not settle the full problem. The Clay Yang–Mills Millennium Problem (a closely related subproblem) remains unsolved.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove that every Yang-Mills field on the four-sphere S4 is either self-dual or anti-self-dual.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^4$ denote the four-dimensional sphere equipped with the standard round metric, and let $P \to S^4$ be a principal $G$-bundle for a compact semisimple Lie group $G$ (e.g. $G = SU(2)$). For a connection $A$ on $P$ with curvature 2-form $F_A$ taking values in the adjoint bundle, the Yang-Mills functional is
$$\mathrm{YM}(A) = \int_{S^4} |F_A|^2 \, d\mathrm{vol}.$$
A connection $A$ is called a Yang-Mills field (or Yang-Mills connection) if it is a critical point of $\mathrm{YM}$, equivalently if it satisfies the Yang-Mills equation $d_A^* F_A = 0$ together with the Bianchi identity $d_A F_A = 0$. Using the Hodge star operator $*$ on 2-forms over $S^4$, the connection $A$ is called self-dual if $*F_A = F_A$ and anti-self-dual if $*F_A = -F_A$.

Decide whether the following statement is true: every Yang-Mills field on $S^4$ is either self-dual or anti-self-dual.
status_search_result: The conjecture is false. Sibner, Sibner, and Uhlenbeck (1989) constructed non-minimal Yang-Mills connections on the trivial SU(2)-bundle over $S^4$ that are neither self-dual nor anti-self-dual. Further non-self-dual Yang-Mills connections were produced by Sadun-Segert, Parker, and others on SU(2)-bundles over $S^4$ with various Chern numbers. Thus the proposed assertion does not hold.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove that, for a fixed Pontryagin number, the moduli space of self-dual Yang-Mills fields on the four-sphere S4 is connected.
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^4$ denote the round 4-sphere, and let $G$ be a compact simple Lie group. Fix a principal $G$-bundle $P \to S^4$, whose topological type is classified by its second Chern number (Pontryagin number) $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. A connection $A$ on $P$ is called self-dual (an instanton) if its curvature 2-form $F_A$ satisfies $*F_A = F_A$, where $*$ is the Hodge star induced by the round metric on $S^4$. Let $\mathcal{M}_k(G)$ denote the moduli space of self-dual connections on $P$ modulo gauge equivalence.

Prove that, for every fixed Pontryagin number $k$, the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_k(G)$ is connected.
status_search_result: For classical gauge groups, the ADHM construction parametrizes self-dual connections on $S^4$ by a connected algebraic variety, and Donaldson established that the moduli space for $G=SU(2)$ at charge $k=1$ is diffeomorphic to an open 5-ball (hence connected); analogous connectedness results follow from ADHM data for $SU(N)$, $Sp(n)$, $SO(N)$. A fully general proof covering all compact simple Lie groups (including exceptional groups) is not as widely cited; the question is listed among Yau's problems and is regarded as essentially known for classical groups but not uniformly settled for all gauge groups.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine the range of validity of the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions used to approximate solutions of Einstein's equations.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein field equations $R_{\mu\nu}=0$ (or with matter sources) on a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold, and the two standard families of asymptotic approximation schemes used to construct approximate solutions:

(a) The post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion, in which the metric is expanded around the flat Minkowski metric as a formal power series in Newton's constant $G$:
$$g_{\mu\nu}=\eta_{\mu\nu}+\sum_{n\geq 1}G^{n}\,h^{(n)}_{\mu\nu},$$
the coefficients $h^{(n)}_{\mu\nu}$ being determined iteratively by solving linearized Einstein equations on Minkowski space with sources built from lower-order coefficients.

(b) The post-Newtonian (PN) expansion, in which (for slowly moving, weakly self-gravitating sources with characteristic velocity $v\ll c$) the metric is expanded in inverse powers of the speed of light $c$:
$$g_{\mu\nu}=\eta_{\mu\nu}+\sum_{n\geq 2}c^{-n}\,k^{(n)}_{\mu\nu},$$
valid in the near zone of the source (distances small compared with the characteristic wavelength of emitted gravitational radiation).

The problem is to determine rigorously the range of validity of these two asymptotic expansions. Specifically:

1. Identify precise conditions on the initial data, matter content, and spacetime region under which the formal series above provide genuine asymptotic approximations (in a mathematically precise sense, e.g. Poincaré-asymptotic) to actual solutions of the Einstein equations.

2. Establish quantitative error bounds: for a truncation at order $N$, give estimates of the form $\|g_{\mu\nu}-g^{(N)}_{\mu\nu}\|\le C_N\,\varepsilon^{N+1}$ in suitable function-space norms, on explicit spacetime domains, where $\varepsilon$ is $G$ or $1/c$ as appropriate.

3. Determine the maximal spacetime region (in terms of distance from the source, time interval, and strength of the gravitational field) on which each expansion remains a faithful approximation, and clarify the matching between the near-zone PN expansion and the far-zone PM expansion.
status_search_result: The rigorous range of validity of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions for solutions of Einstein's equations remains an open problem. While Damour–Schäfer and others showed PN expansions are asymptotic in a formal sense, divergences appear from 4PN order in harmonic coordinates, and no global rigorous error estimates or matched-asymptotic theorems are established. Recent reviews (Blanchet's Living Reviews on PN theory, 2024) and works on resummation (2025) continue to treat validity and convergence as unresolved.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove rigorously that there exists a limit in which solutions of Einstein's equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.
self_contained_problem:
Give a rigorous mathematical proof that Newtonian gravity arises as a well-defined limit of general relativity. Concretely: introduce a one-parameter family of Lorentzian spacetimes $(M, g_\lambda, T_\lambda)$, indexed by a parameter $\lambda \geq 0$ (interpreted as $1/c^2$, where $c$ is the speed of light), each satisfying the Einstein field equations
$$\mathrm{Ric}(g_\lambda) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g_\lambda)\, g_\lambda = 8\pi\, T_\lambda$$
for $\lambda > 0$, where $T_\lambda$ is a suitable matter stress-energy tensor. Formulate precise regularity, asymptotic, and matter conditions on the family $\{(M, g_\lambda, T_\lambda)\}_{\lambda > 0}$ under which, as $\lambda \to 0^+$, the metrics, connections, and matter fields converge (in an appropriate topology) to a limiting structure $(M, h, t, \nabla, \rho)$ describing a Newton–Cartan / Newtonian spacetime, where:
- $t : M \to \mathbb{R}$ is an absolute time function with level sets being spacelike hypersurfaces,
- $h$ is a degenerate "spatial" cometric of signature $(0,+,+,+)$ with kernel spanned by $dt$,
- $\nabla$ is a torsion-free connection compatible with $t$ and $h$,
- $\rho : M \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ is a mass density,
and the limiting structure satisfies the Newton–Cartan field equation
$$\mathrm{Ric}(\nabla) = 4\pi\rho\, dt \otimes dt$$
together with the appropriate Trautman/Newton curvature conditions. Prove the existence of nontrivial families realizing such a limit (beyond known special examples), and establish convergence theorems guaranteeing that solutions of the Einstein equations reduce, in this limit, to solutions of Newtonian gravity.
status_search_result: Ehlers's frame theory provides a rigorous framework for the Newtonian limit, and a number of partial results exist: examples of one-parameter families of relativistic spacetimes with a Newtonian limit have been constructed (e.g., Lottermoser, Rendall, Oliynyk, Heilig), and post-Newtonian expansions have been justified rigorously in various settings. However, a fully general rigorous existence theorem for families of solutions of Einstein's equations converging to arbitrary Newtonian spacetimes is not yet established, so the problem is widely regarded as only partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove that a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R × M^3.
self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^4, g)$ be a cosmological spacetime, meaning a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian 4-manifold admitting a compact Cauchy hypersurface. Assume that $(M, g)$ satisfies the timelike convergence condition, i.e., the Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(v, v) \geq 0$ for every timelike vector $v \in TM$. Prove that one of the following holds:

(a) $(M, g)$ is timelike geodesically incomplete; or

(b) $(M, g)$ splits isometrically as a metric product $(\mathbb{R} \times M^3,\, -dt^2 \oplus h)$, where $(M^3, h)$ is a compact Riemannian 3-manifold (so the spacetime is static).
status_search_result: Known as Bartnik's splitting conjecture (1988). original_question: Find an exact solution of Einstein's equations that represents two orbiting bodies, and determine whether the two-body system is unstable in Einstein gravity.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture in general relativity: for generic initial data for the evolution problem, naked singularities should not occur.
self_contained_problem:
Working within the framework of classical general relativity, consider the Einstein field equations as an initial-value (Cauchy) problem: one specifies initial data consisting of a 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold (Σ, h) together with a symmetric 2-tensor K on Σ (representing the induced metric and extrinsic curvature of an embedded spacelike hypersurface) and matter data satisfying suitable energy conditions and the Einstein constraint equations. The maximal globally hyperbolic development of such data is a Lorentzian 4-manifold (M, g) solving the Einstein equations with Σ as a Cauchy surface.

A spacetime (M, g) is said to contain a naked singularity if there exists a singular boundary point (e.g., where curvature invariants diverge or geodesic incompleteness occurs) that is visible to some observer at future null infinity—equivalently, the future null infinity is not complete, or there is a future-inextendible causal curve from the singular set reaching observers outside any event horizon.

Formulate and prove the following statement (the weak cosmic censorship conjecture): For generic asymptotically flat initial data (in some suitable topology on the space of admissible initial data) for the Einstein evolution equations coupled to physically reasonable matter, the maximal Cauchy development possesses a complete future null infinity; equivalently, no naked singularities arise from generic regular initial data. Both an appropriate precise formulation (specifying the genericity condition, the matter model, the asymptotic conditions, and the notion of completeness of null infinity) and a proof are required.
status_search_result: The weak cosmic censorship conjecture, originally proposed by Penrose in 1969, remains a major open problem in mathematical general relativity. While partial results exist (e.g., Christodoulou's proof for the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field system, and various results on trapped surface formation and stability of black holes), no general proof is known, and even a universally accepted precise formulation is lacking. As of recent surveys and research up to 2026, the conjecture is still considered open.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Let M be a three-dimensional compact manifold. Prove that, for generic vacuum initial data on M, the maximal vacuum Cauchy development equals the maximal vacuum extension of M.
self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth three-dimensional manifold. A vacuum initial data set on $M$ consists of a Riemannian metric $g$ and a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor $K$ on $M$ satisfying the vacuum constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\operatorname{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_g K - d(\operatorname{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R(g)$ denotes the scalar curvature of $g$. To any such initial data set there is associated a maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum Cauchy development: a Ricci-flat Lorentzian 4-manifold $(\widetilde{M}, \widetilde{g})$ (i.e. $\operatorname{Ric}(\widetilde{g})=0$) in which $(M,g,K)$ embeds as a Cauchy hypersurface with induced metric $g$ and second fundamental form $K$, and which is maximal among all such globally hyperbolic developments. A maximal vacuum extension of $M$ is a Ricci-flat Lorentzian 4-manifold containing $(M,g,K)$ as an embedded spacelike hypersurface (not necessarily Cauchy) which is maximal with respect to isometric extension.

Prove (or disprove) the following: for a generic vacuum initial data set $(g,K)$ on $M$, the maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum Cauchy development of $(M,g,K)$ coincides with the maximal vacuum extension of $(M,g,K)$. Equivalently, generically the maximal Cauchy development admits no proper Ricci-flat Lorentzian extension.

status_search_result: This is a formulation of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture for closed cosmological vacuum spacetimes. It remains open in general. Partial results exist, notably the proof that vacuum spacetimes with a compact Cauchy horizon of constant nonzero surface gravity admit a Killing field (Moncrief–Isenberg conjecture), implying genericity-style obstructions to extension in that special case, and various results under symmetry assumptions. paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Either prove the Penrose inequality in full generality or produce a counterexample to it.
self_contained_problem:
Let (M, g, k) be an asymptotically flat initial data set for the Einstein equations of general relativity. That is, M is a 3-dimensional smooth manifold equipped with a complete Riemannian metric g and a symmetric (0,2)-tensor k (the second fundamental form of M as a spacelike hypersurface in a Lorentzian spacetime), such that outside a compact set M is diffeomorphic to the complement of a ball in R^3 and g and k satisfy standard asymptotic flatness decay conditions ensuring that the ADM mass m_ADM is well defined. Let A denote the area of the outermost apparent horizon in (M, g, k) (the outermost surface on which the future-outgoing null expansion vanishes, viewed as the boundary of the trapped region).

The Penrose inequality asserts that
   m_ADM ≥ sqrt( A / (16π) ).

Problem: Either prove this inequality in the full generality stated above (without symmetry, time-symmetry, maximality of the slice, or other restrictive assumptions on the initial data), or exhibit an asymptotically flat initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition for which the inequality fails.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: For collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data; also prove existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions such as Bianchi type IX solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov equations, and investigate the large-initial-data regime.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Vlasov system, which couples the Einstein field equations of general relativity to the relativistic Vlasov equation describing a collisionless ensemble of particles. The unknowns are a 4-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ and a non-negative distribution function $f$ on the mass shell in the cotangent bundle of $M$, satisfying

(i) the Vlasov equation: $f$ is constant along the geodesic flow on the mass shell, and

(ii) the Einstein equations $R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}R\, g_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi T_{\mu\nu}$, where the energy-momentum tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ is the second momentum of $f$ on the mass shell.

Address the following:

1. (Inhomogeneous small data) Prove a global-in-time existence theorem for classical solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system (and more generally for collisionless matter models coupled to Einstein's equations) for spatially inhomogeneous initial data that are sufficiently small in a suitable norm.

2. (Homogeneous case) Prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov system, in particular for solutions of Bianchi type IX symmetry (the case of a homogeneous spatial slicing with isometry group $SU(2)$).

3. (Large data) Investigate the dynamical behavior of these solutions in the regime of large initial data, including questions of global existence, formation of singularities, and asymptotic behavior toward the past and the future.
status_search_result: Survey literature on the Einstein–Vlasov system (Andréasson's Living Reviews articles) and subsequent works confirm partial results: small-data global existence is known in special symmetry classes (e.g., surface symmetry, asymptotically flat with spherical symmetry, cosmological with positive cosmological constant), and Bianchi I/II/etc. homogeneous models have been treated, but the general spatially inhomogeneous small-data problem and the full Bianchi type IX existence/uniqueness with large-data dynamics remain open. Recent work (e.g., Lee, Heinzle–Uggla, Ringström) has advanced understanding but has not closed the problem.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, with weakly turbulent transfer of energy to high frequencies leading to black-hole formation, persists or changes in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein equations with negative cosmological constant Λ < 0, whose maximally symmetric vacuum solution is Anti–de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. It has been conjectured that AdS spacetime is nonlinearly unstable: for generic, arbitrarily small smooth perturbations of the AdS initial data, the evolution exhibits a weakly turbulent transfer of energy from low to high frequencies (a direct cascade in the spectrum of linear AdS normal modes), and eventually leads to the formation of a black hole. This conjecture has been studied in detail in the case of a self-gravitating massless scalar field under the assumption of spherical symmetry, where reflecting boundary conditions are imposed at conformal infinity.

Problem. Determine whether this weakly turbulent nonlinear instability mechanism, and the associated black-hole formation, persists or is qualitatively modified in settings more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse — for instance, for purely gravitational perturbations (where spherical symmetry is necessarily broken), for perturbations breaking axial symmetry, for other matter models, or around rotating (Kerr–AdS) backgrounds. Specifically, characterize whether generic small perturbations in these more general settings still trigger a turbulent cascade culminating in horizon formation, or whether new phenomena (e.g., islands of stability, alternative endpoints, or different cascade structures such as inverse cascades) arise.
status_search_result: The problem is the subject of active research. Beyond spherical symmetry, work by Dias, Horowitz, Santos and collaborators (2016, 2017) showed that purely gravitational perturbations of AdS behave qualitatively differently from spherically symmetric scalar collapse: not all normal modes extend to periodic geons, single-mode seeds can produce secular resonances, and both direct and inverse cascades can appear. Moschidis (2017–2020) gave a rigorous proof of AdS instability for the Einstein–massless Vlasov system in spherical symmetry. A 2025 study established nonlinear instability of slowly rotating Kerr–AdS with non-axisymmetric endpoints. Thus partial progress exists, but a full understanding of nonlinear AdS instability in general (non-symmetric, vacuum gravitational) settings remains open.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine the uniqueness classification of black holes in higher-dimensional spacetimes.
self_contained_problem:
Let $D \geq 5$ and consider $D$-dimensional stationary, asymptotically flat solutions $(M, g)$ of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ (or, more generally, of the Einstein–Maxwell equations) that contain a regular event horizon (a "black hole" spacetime). In four dimensions, the classical uniqueness theorems show that any such regular, stationary, asymptotically flat electrovacuum black hole is characterized by its mass, angular momentum, and electric charge (the Kerr–Newman family). In higher dimensions this fails: the Myers–Perry rotating black holes, the Emparan–Reall black rings, and other solutions can share the same conserved asymptotic charges yet be geometrically distinct, and additional horizon topologies $S^{D-2}$, $S^1 \times S^{D-3}$, etc., are possible.

Problem. Provide a complete classification (uniqueness theorem) for stationary, asymptotically flat black hole solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations in dimension $D \geq 5$: determine the full list of invariants (mass, independent angular momenta, horizon topology, rod structure / interval structure on the orbit space, and any further data) that uniquely characterize such a solution up to isometry, and prove that any regular stationary asymptotically flat black hole spacetime is determined by these invariants. Extend the classification to the Einstein–Maxwell case and, where possible, to non‑asymptotically‑flat settings (e.g. Kaluza–Klein, asymptotically (anti–)de Sitter) in higher dimensions.
status_search_result: The general classification of stationary black holes in dimensions $D \geq 5$ remains an open problem. Uniqueness is established for static asymptotically flat vacuum/electrovacuum black holes in all dimensions and for stationary axisymmetric vacuum solutions in $D=5$ with given rod structure, but no full uniqueness theorem is known for general stationary higher-dimensional black holes (e.g. with fewer commuting Killing vectors, charged rotating, or asymptotically (A)dS cases). Recent work (e.g. Kaluza–Klein static uniqueness, 2025) continues to address sub-cases.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine the stability properties of black holes in higher-dimensional spacetimes.
self_contained_problem:
Consider, for each integer $d\ge 5$, vacuum (or electrovacuum/cosmological-constant) black hole solutions of the Einstein equations on a $d$-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime. Examples include the higher-dimensional Schwarzschild–Tangherlini family, the Myers–Perry rotating black holes, charged generalizations, black holes with non-zero cosmological constant (Schwarzschild–(A)dS, Kerr–(A)dS), and black holes with non-spherical horizon topology such as black rings and black strings.

For each such family, determine whether the solution is dynamically stable. Concretely:

(a) Linear (mode) stability: Show whether every solution of the linearized Einstein equations around the background, with suitable boundary/asymptotic conditions, remains uniformly bounded in time. Equivalently, determine whether the spectrum of the relevant perturbation operator on the space of admissible perturbations (tensor, vector, and scalar types in the Kodama–Ishibashi decomposition) contains any modes with growth in time.

(b) Nonlinear stability: Determine whether small perturbations of initial data for the background, evolved under the full Einstein equations, asymptote back to a member of the same family (possibly with shifted parameters), in analogy with the nonlinear stability of Minkowski space and of the Kerr family in four dimensions.

Provide a complete classification across all values of $d\ge 5$, all rotation parameters (including ultraspinning regimes for $d\ge 6$), all charges, and all admissible horizon topologies, of which higher-dimensional black hole solutions are stable and which are unstable, together with proofs.

status_search_result: Partial results exist: higher-dimensional Schwarzschild (and Schwarzschild–(A)dS) black holes have been shown to be linearly stable against tensor, vector, and scalar perturbations via S-deformation of master equations (Ishibashi–Kodama and others). Instabilities have been identified in ultraspinning Myers–Perry black holes for $d\ge 6$ and in black strings (Gregory–Laflamme). However, linear and nonlinear stability for general rotating Myers–Perry black holes, charged solutions, and non-spherical horizon topologies remain largely open, as the gravitational perturbation equations do not decouple analogously to the Kerr case.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine whether singularity-resolution results proved in spatially homogeneous loop quantum gravity or loop quantum cosmology can be extended and proved in more general, less symmetry-reduced settings.
self_contained_problem:
In loop quantum gravity (LQG), a background-independent canonical quantization of general relativity based on holonomies of an SU(2) connection and conjugate flux variables, and in its symmetry-reduced cousin loop quantum cosmology (LQC), classical curvature singularities (such as the big-bang singularity of homogeneous and isotropic FLRW models) are known to be resolved at the quantum level: the quantum evolution remains well-defined and extends across the would-be singularity, typically replacing it by a quantum bounce or a regular transition surface. These results have been established in spatially homogeneous (and often isotropic) minisuperspace truncations of gravity coupled to matter.

Problem. Determine whether the singularity-resolution mechanisms established in spatially homogeneous LQC/LQG models can be rigorously extended to less symmetric, more general settings — for instance to midisuperspace models such as spherically symmetric or Gowdy spacetimes, to inhomogeneous cosmological perturbations around a homogeneous background, and ultimately to the full inhomogeneous loop-quantized theory. Specifically, formulate and prove (or disprove) a theorem stating that, in such broader settings, classical curvature singularities of generic solutions are replaced by a regular quantum evolution.
status_search_result: Reviews and recent work indicate this remains an active open question. Singularity resolution is well-established in homogeneous LQC, and partial progress exists in midisuperspace models (e.g., spherically symmetric loop quantizations replacing the Schwarzschild singularity by a transition surface). However, extending these results to genuinely inhomogeneous settings and full LQG remains unresolved, with indications that bounces appear less robustly in inhomogeneous quantizations.

original_question: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system is exactly the Mixmaster attractor, rather than merely a subset of it.

rather than being a proper subset of A.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Prove the BKL locality conjecture for general inhomogeneous spacetimes approaching a generic spacelike singularity.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ that is a solution of the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$ (or, more generally, of the Einstein equations coupled to standard matter), and assume that $(M,g)$ develops a generic spacelike singularity, i.e. a singular boundary along which a foliation by spacelike hypersurfaces $\{\Sigma_t\}$ has $t\to 0^+$ corresponding to curvature blow-up.

The Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz (BKL) locality conjecture asserts that, as $t\to 0^+$, spatial derivatives of the metric become negligible compared with time derivatives, so that the Einstein evolution equations effectively decouple at each spatial point $x\in\Sigma_t$ and reduce to a system of ordinary differential equations in $t$ (the "Mixmaster" / Bianchi IX dynamics in the vacuum case). Equivalently, the asymptotic behaviour of the metric near the singularity should, at each spatial point, be governed by the corresponding spatially homogeneous model, with the spatial point appearing only parametrically.

Problem: Prove the BKL locality conjecture for general (i.e. not assumed to possess any continuous spatial symmetry) inhomogeneous spacetimes approaching a generic spacelike singularity. That is, establish rigorously that for an open set of generic initial data leading to a spacelike singularity, the resulting solution of the Einstein equations satisfies, in a precise asymptotic sense as one approaches the singularity, the local decoupling and ODE-dominated behaviour described above.
status_search_result: The BKL locality conjecture remains unproven in the general inhomogeneous setting. Rigorous results exist only in symmetric reductions (e.g. Gowdy spacetimes, surface-symmetric Einstein–Maxwell–scalar field models) or for matter that suppresses oscillations (massless scalar field / stiff fluid), where convergence to truncated/velocity-dominated dynamics has been established. Numerical and heuristic evidence as of recent work continues to support the conjecture, but a full proof for generic vacuum inhomogeneous spacetimes is still lacking.

original_question: Prove that spike structures occur near generic cosmological singularities and determine how those spikes affect any eventual proof of generic singularity behavior.
self_contained_problem:
Consider solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations on a globally hyperbolic spacetime that develop a spacelike singularity to the past. The Belinskii–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz (BKL) conjecture asserts that for generic initial data, the approach to such a singularity is local, vacuum-dominated, and oscillatory: at each spatial point the geometry undergoes an infinite sequence of Kasner epochs whose successive Kasner exponents are governed (in suitable scale-invariant variables) by an ODE map, with spatial derivative terms in Einstein's equations becoming negligible compared with time derivative terms.

Within this framework, "spikes" are spatial features where the asymptotic Kasner exponents fail to vary continuously: at exceptional spatial points the system follows a different sequence of Kasner epochs from that of nearby points, so that as the singularity is approached the spatial profile of curvature invariants and frame variables develops increasingly narrow and tall transient structures that are not captured by the purely local BKL ODE description.

(a) (Existence of spikes.) (b) (Effect on a generic singularity proof.) Determine precisely how the presence of such spikes must be incorporated into, or modifies, any rigorous proof that generic solutions of the Einstein equations exhibit BKL-type oscillatory behavior on approach to a spacelike singularity; in particular, give a description of the dynamics in spike neighborhoods that is compatible with, and can be combined with, the local BKL ODE asymptotics on the complementary (non-spike) set so as to yield a complete proof of generic singularity behavior.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Determine whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity.
self_contained_problem:
Background. In general relativity, a cosmological spacetime is said to have an isotropic singularity (in the sense of Goode–Wainwright) if its physical metric $g_{ab}$ is conformally related to a metric $\tilde g_{ab}$ that is regular on an initial spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma$, via $g_{ab} = \Omega^2(\tau)\,\tilde g_{ab}$, with a conformal factor $\Omega(\tau)$ satisfying $\Omega(\tau) \to 0$ as $\tau \to \tau_0$ (the singularity), $\Omega(\tau) > 0$ for $\tau > \tau_0$, and suitable regularity conditions ensuring that the Weyl tensor of $g_{ab}$ remains bounded (vanishes after rescaling) at the singular hypersurface. Such singularities encode a mathematical version of Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis: the initial cosmological singularity is, after conformal rescaling, a regular spacelike hypersurface on which the rescaled Weyl tensor vanishes.

By a "modified theory of gravity" we mean any geometric theory of gravitation whose field equations differ from the Einstein equations $G_{ab} = T_{ab}$; standard examples include $f(R)$ theories, scalar–tensor theories (e.g. Brans–Dicke), Gauss–Bonnet and Lovelock gravity, and Einstein–æther type theories. Fix such a theory and a reasonable class of matter models satisfying standard energy conditions.

Question. Determine whether, in this modified theory of gravity, isotropic singularities are typical (generic) among cosmological solutions developing an initial spacelike singularity. More precisely: is the set of initial data (in a suitable function-space topology on the space of admissible Cauchy data) that gives rise to past singularities of isotropic type non-meagre / of positive measure / open / generic, in the sense that perturbations of an isotropic-singularity solution within the theory continue to develop isotropic singularities? Provide either a proof of genericity or a construction showing isotropic singularities are non-generic in the chosen modified gravity theory.
status_search_result: The question of whether isotropic singularities (in the Goode–Wainwright sense, formalizing Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis) are generic in modified theories of gravity does not appear to have been resolved. Existing work establishes the Weyl curvature hypothesis in certain quasi-regular spacetime classes within general relativity, but no general result is known for typical modified gravity theories, and quantum-gravity-inspired modifications are noted as potentially obstructing the hypothesis.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Resolve the black hole information paradox.
self_contained_problem: Consider a quantum field theory on a curved spacetime background that contains a black hole formed by gravitational collapse from an initial pure quantum state. According to Hawking's semiclassical analysis, the black hole emits thermal radiation (Hawking radiation) and eventually evaporates completely. The resulting radiation appears to be in a mixed thermal state, suggesting that an initially pure quantum state evolves into a mixed state, in apparent violation of the unitarity of quantum mechanics. The black hole information paradox asks: does the process of black hole formation and complete evaporation preserve quantum information (i.e., is the overall evolution unitary), and if so, by what precise mechanism is the information carried out, encoded, or recovered from the Hawking radiation? Provide a mathematically consistent framework — compatible with both general relativity in the appropriate regime and the principles of quantum mechanics — that resolves this apparent conflict, including a derivation of how the von Neumann entropy of the radiation evolves (the Page curve) and an explicit account of how correlations between early and late Hawking radiation arise or how information otherwise escapes, or alternatively, demonstrate rigorously that unitarity must be abandoned.
status_search_result: The black hole information paradox remains an actively debated open problem. Recent developments (2019–2023), including the computation of the Page curve via the "island formula" using replica wormholes and the quantum extremal surface prescription, have given strong evidence that gravitational entropy calculations are consistent with unitarity. However, a complete, generally accepted mechanism for information recovery in physical black holes is still lacking, and the paradox is not considered fully resolved.

original_question: Resolve the cosmological constant problem and the problem of dark energy.
self_contained_problem:
In the framework of general relativity coupled to quantum field theory, the Einstein field equations with a cosmological constant Λ read

  R_{μν} − (1/2) g_{μν} R + Λ g_{μν} = 8πG T_{μν},

where g_{μν} is the spacetime metric, R_{μν} the Ricci tensor, R its trace, G Newton's constant, and T_{μν} the stress-energy tensor of matter. Observations of the accelerated expansion of the universe yield an effective value Λ_obs corresponding to a vacuum energy density ρ_Λ ≈ 10^{−47} GeV^4. A naive quantum field theoretic estimate of the zero-point energy of the Standard Model fields, regulated at the Planck scale M_P, gives a vacuum energy density ρ_vac ∼ M_P^4 ≈ 10^{72} GeV^4, exceeding ρ_Λ by roughly 120 orders of magnitude.

(ii) the systematic bias in Bayesian parameter inference, induced by the difference between the model and the true waveform, is smaller than the statistical uncertainty for signals at the sensitivity of current and planned gravitational-wave detectors.

Equivalently, construct a family of waveform templates $\{h(t;\lambda)\}$ such that for every $\lambda$ in the physical domain, the model error is dominated by detector noise and statistical fluctuations rather than by theoretical modeling uncertainty.

paper_title: Open problems in mathematical physics
original_question: Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse within general relativity.
self_contained_problem:
Consider classical general relativity coupled to a matter model (for instance a massless scalar field minimally coupled to gravity, a perfect fluid, the Yang–Mills field, or vacuum gravity), and consider one-parameter families of smooth asymptotically flat initial data, parametrized by p, that interpolate between dispersion (no black hole formed in the Cauchy development) for p < p* and black hole formation for p > p*. Numerical evidence (originating from the spherically symmetric massless scalar field) shows that near the threshold p = p* one observes:

(i) Universality: the late-time near-threshold evolution is independent of the chosen family.
(ii) Power-law scaling of the black-hole mass: M_BH ∝ (p − p*)^γ for p ↘ p*, with a critical exponent γ that depends only on the matter model.
(iii) Self-similarity (discrete or continuous) of the threshold solution, with echoing periods that are matter-model dependent.

These phenomena are heuristically explained by codimension-one attractors in the infinite-dimensional phase space of solutions, which are exactly self-similar.

Problem. Develop a rigorous mathematical understanding of critical phenomena in gravitational collapse within general relativity. In particular:

(a) Prove existence, uniqueness, and (codimension-one) stability of the critical (self-similar) threshold solutions for canonical matter models, and derive the critical exponent γ and any echoing period Δ analytically.
(b) Determine whether critical behavior at the black-hole threshold persists beyond spherical symmetry, including the vacuum case, and identify the dependence (if any) of γ and Δ on the matter content and symmetry assumptions.
(c) Establish rigorously the connection between the threshold behavior and the formation of arbitrarily large curvatures visible from infinity, and clarify its implications for weak cosmic censorship.
status_search_result: Surveys and recent reviews of critical phenomena in gravitational collapse (Gundlach–Martín-García Living Reviews, and a 2025 review on arXiv:2507.07636) confirm that, although numerical and heuristic understanding has advanced considerably since Choptuik's discovery, a rigorous mathematical theory is lacking. In particular it remains unclear how universal the phenomena are with respect to matter content and beyond spherical symmetry (including the vacuum case), and analytic derivations of the critical exponent and echoing period are not available. The problem is therefore still considered open.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety over C. Must one of the following two alternatives always hold: either X is uniruled, or X is birational to a projective variety X_min such that X_min is Q-factorial, has only terminal singularities, and its canonical divisor K_{X_min} is nef?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. Recall that:

- $X$ is called uniruled if there exists a variety $Y$ of dimension $\dim X - 1$ and a dominant rational map $Y \times \mathbb{P}^1 \dashrightarrow X$.
- A normal projective variety $X_{\min}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial if every Weil divisor on $X_{\min}$ has an integer multiple that is Cartier.
- $X_{\min}$ has only terminal singularities if there exists a resolution $f : \widetilde{X} \to X_{\min}$ such that $K_{X_{\min}}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier and, writing $K_{\widetilde{X}} = f^{*}K_{X_{\min}} + \sum a_i E_i$ for the exceptional divisors $E_i$, all discrepancies satisfy $a_i > 0$.
- A $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor $D$ on a projective variety is nef if $D \cdot C \geq 0$ for every irreducible projective curve $C$.

Prove or disprove: at least one of the following two alternatives must hold.
(1) $X$ is uniruled.
(2) There exists a projective variety $X_{\min}$ birational to $X$ such that $X_{\min}$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial, has only terminal singularities, and the canonical divisor $K_{X_{\min}}$ is nef.
status_search_result: The minimal model conjecture is established in dimension $\leq 3$ (Mori, Kawamata, Kollár, Shokurov), and Birkar–Cascini–Hacon–McKernan (2010) proved existence of minimal models for smooth projective varieties of general type in all dimensions, as well as the uniruledness dichotomy modulo abundance assumptions in some cases. The full conjecture in dimension $\geq 4$ for varieties not of general type (equivalently, the non-uniruled case with intermediate Kodaira dimension) remains open as of 2026.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let (X, D) be a smooth projective variety such that K_X + D is pseudoeffective. Is the asymptotic growth rate of h^0(X, m(K_X + D)) equal to the asymptotic growth rate obtained after twisting by an arbitrary ample line bundle A, namely does limsup_{m→∞} log h^0(X, m(K_X + D)) / log m equal sup_A limsup_{m→∞} log h^0(X, A + m(K_X + D)) / log m, where m ranges over positive integers for which m(K_X + D) is Cartier?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and let $D$ be a divisor on $X$ such that $(X,D)$ is a log smooth pair and $K_X + D$ is pseudoeffective (i.e., its numerical class lies in the closure of the cone generated by effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisors). For a Cartier divisor $L$ on $X$, let $h^0(X,L) = \dim_{\mathbb{C}} H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X(L))$.

Define the Iitaka-type asymptotic invariant
$$\kappa_-(K_X+D) \;=\; \limsup_{m \to \infty,\; m(K_X+D)\ \text{Cartier}} \frac{\log h^0\!\bigl(X, m(K_X+D)\bigr)}{\log m},$$
and the numerical Iitaka-type invariant
$$\kappa_\sigma(K_X+D) \;=\; \sup_{A} \;\limsup_{m \to \infty,\; m(K_X+D)\ \text{Cartier}} \frac{\log h^0\!\bigl(X, A + m(K_X+D)\bigr)}{\log m},$$
where $A$ ranges over all ample line bundles on $X$.

Prove or disprove: under the above hypotheses one always has
$$\kappa_-(K_X+D) \;=\; \kappa_\sigma(K_X+D).$$
status_search_result: This is a form of the abundance/numerical-Kodaira-dimension equality for log canonical pairs (sometimes stated as $\kappa = \kappa_\sigma$ for $K_X+D$ pseudoeffective). It is known in low dimension and in special cases (e.g. dim $\le 3$, varieties of general type, log minimal models with good abundance) but remains open in general dimensions; it is widely regarded as one of the central open conjectures in birational geometry.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let f: X → S be a surjective proper Kähler morphism with connected fibers between connected complex manifolds, and let (L, h_L) be a singular Hermitian Q-line bundle on X with semipositive curvature such that for every smooth fiber X_s over s in S^o, the restriction (L, h_L)|_{X_s} is well defined, Kawamata log terminal, and K_{X_s} + L|_{X_s} is pseudoeffective. If h_{min,X/S}(L, h_L) is defined fiberwise from the relative maximal volume form dV_{max,X/S}(L, h_L), does this metric extend from f^{-1}(S^o) to a singular Hermitian metric on K_{X/S} + L over all of X with semipositive curvature?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f: X \to S$ be a surjective proper Kähler morphism with connected fibers between connected complex manifolds, and let $S^o \subseteq S$ denote the locus over which $f$ is smooth. Let $(L, h_L)$ be a singular Hermitian $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle on $X$ whose curvature current is semipositive, and assume that for every $s \in S^o$ the restriction $(L, h_L)|_{X_s}$ is well defined, the pair $(X_s, L|_{X_s})$ is Kawamata log terminal (i.e., the local weights $\varphi$ of $h_L$ satisfy $e^{-\varphi} \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on $X_s$), and $K_{X_s} + L|_{X_s}$ is pseudoeffective.

For each $s \in S^o$, define the relative maximal volume form $dV_{\max, X/S}(L, h_L)$ fiberwise by
$$dV_{\max, X_s}(L|_{X_s}, h_L|_{X_s}) = \sup\bigl\{\,|\sigma|^{2/m}\,h_L^{1/m} : m \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0},\ \sigma \in H^0(X_s, m(K_{X_s}+L|_{X_s})\otimes \mathcal{I}(h_L^m|_{X_s})),\ \tfrac{1}{m}\!\int_{X_s}\!|\sigma|^{2/m}h_L^{1/m} \leq 1\,\bigr\},$$
where the supremum is taken in the sense of upper envelopes of singular volume forms, and let $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ be the associated singular Hermitian metric on $(K_{X/S} + L)|_{f^{-1}(S^o)}$ determined by $dV_{\max, X/S}(L, h_L)$ in the usual way (so that the curvature of $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ on $f^{-1}(S^o)$ is semipositive).

Question: does $h_{\min, X/S}(L, h_L)$ extend from $f^{-1}(S^o)$ to a singular Hermitian metric on the line bundle $K_{X/S} + L$ over all of $X$ whose curvature current is semipositive?
category_tag: Singular Hermitian metrics on relative canonical bundles
status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture about the extension of the relative minimal singular Hermitian metric on $K_{X/S}+L$ to the whole base, with semipositive curvature. Related results of Tsuji, Berndtsson-Păun, and others establish semipositivity over the smooth locus and in various settings, but a search did not locate a definitive proof of this precise extension statement in the stated generality. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety and let (L, h_L) be a pseudoeffective Kawamata log terminal line bundle on X. Are the three canonical singular metrics on K_X + L defined in the paper always equal, namely does \hat h_can(L, h_L) = \hat h_min(L, h_L) = h_min(L, h_L) hold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $(L,h_L)$ be a singular Hermitian line bundle on $X$ that is pseudoeffective (i.e. the curvature current $\Theta_{h_L} = -\sqrt{-1}\,\partial\bar\partial\log h_L \geq 0$) and Kawamata log terminal (KLT) in the sense that the multiplier ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}(h_L)$ equals $\mathcal{O}_X$. On the adjoint line bundle $K_X + L$ one can construct three canonical singular Hermitian metrics:

(i) The dynamical canonical metric $\hat h_{\mathrm{can}}(L,h_L)$, obtained as the limit of the normalized iteration
$$h_{m+1} = \left(K(mh_m \cdot h_L^{-1})\right)^{-1/m},$$
where $K(\cdot)$ denotes the diagonal of the Bergman kernel of $H^0(X, m(K_X+L))$ with respect to the indicated weight, started from any smooth positively curved initial metric.

(ii) The supercanonical (minimal-among-canonical) metric $\hat h_{\min}(L,h_L)$ defined as the upper envelope
$$\hat h_{\min}(L,h_L)^{-1}(x) = \sup\{|\sigma(x)|^2 : \sigma \in H^0(X, m(K_X+L)), \ m \geq 1,\ \tfrac{1}{m}\int_X |\sigma|^{2/m} h_L \leq 1\},$$
suitably normalized.

(iii) The minimal singular metric $h_{\min}(L,h_L)$ on $K_X+L$, namely a singular Hermitian metric with semipositive curvature current whose local weight is maximal (in the sense of the partial order of plurisubharmonic functions) among all such metrics on $K_X+L$.

Prove or disprove: for every such $X$ and every pseudoeffective KLT singular Hermitian line bundle $(L,h_L)$ on $X$, the identities
$$\hat h_{\mathrm{can}}(L,h_L) \;=\; \hat h_{\min}(L,h_L) \;=\; h_{\min}(L,h_L)$$
hold.
category_tag: Canonical singular Hermitian metrics on adjoint line bundles
status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the equality of these three canonical singular metrics on $K_X+L$ for arbitrary pseudoeffective KLT line bundles. Related work on canonical/Bergman-kernel metrics and singular Kähler-Einstein metrics exists, but no source clearly settles the full equality conjecture, so the current status is taken to be unknown.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety and let D be an effective Q-divisor such that (X, D) is Kawamata log terminal. Let σ_D be a nontrivial multivalued holomorphic section with divisor D and set h_D := |σ_D|^{-2}. Assuming K_X + D is pseudoeffective, must every extremal volume form dV with respect to (D, h_D) satisfy that dV ⊗ h_D^{-1} is generically pluriharmonic, meaning the current \sqrt{-1}Θ_{dV^{-1}·h_D} has vanishing absolutely continuous part, and must K_X + D then be Q-effective?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and let $D$ be an effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$ such that the pair $(X,D)$ is Kawamata log terminal (KLT); that is, for some (equivalently every) log resolution $\mu: Y \to X$ with $\mu^*(K_X+D) = K_Y + \sum a_i E_i$ over a simple normal crossing divisor, all coefficients satisfy $a_i < 1$.

Choose a nontrivial multivalued holomorphic section $\sigma_D$ of the $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle associated with $D$ whose divisor equals $D$, and set the (singular) Hermitian metric
$$h_D := |\sigma_D|^{-2}$$
on the $\mathbb{Q}$-line bundle $\mathcal{O}_X(D)$. A volume form $dV$ on $X$ with at worst KLT-type singularities along $D$ is called extremal with respect to $(D,h_D)$ if it has minimal singularities among (suitably normalized) singular volume forms whose associated curvature current
$$\sqrt{-1}\,\Theta_{dV^{-1}\cdot h_D}$$
representing $c_1(K_X+D)$ is a positive closed current.

Assume that $K_X+D$ is pseudoeffective. Prove or disprove:

(1) For every extremal volume form $dV$ with respect to $(D,h_D)$, the section $dV \otimes h_D^{-1}$ is generically pluriharmonic, in the sense that the absolutely continuous part of the curvature current $\sqrt{-1}\,\Theta_{dV^{-1}\cdot h_D}$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure, in the sense of Siu's decomposition) vanishes identically.

(2) $K_X+D$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-effective, i.e., some positive integral multiple $m(K_X+D)$ is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor.
category_tag: Extremal volume forms and abundance for KLT pairs
status_search_result: The statement is a strong analytic refinement of the (log) abundance conjecture for KLT pairs with pseudoeffective log canonical class. Even the conclusion (2) — $\mathbb{Q}$-effectivity of $K_X+D$ under pseudoeffectiveness — is the nonvanishing/abundance conjecture in the KLT setting and is widely regarded as open in general (known in dimension $\le 3$ and in various special cases). No source was found establishing the full conjecture, including the generic pluriharmonicity of extremal volume forms.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry

Must X have nonnegative Kodaira dimension, and must the paper's canonical and maximal volume forms all coincide up to a positive constant, namely \hat dV_can = \hat dV_max = dV_max = C · dμ_can for some C > 0?

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: For the punctured disk Δ* = { t in C | 0 < |t| < 1 }, does the inverse canonical metric satisfy the asymptotic upper bound h_{can,Δ*}^{-1} = O( (\sqrt{-1} dt ∧ dar t) / (|t|^2 (log |t|)^2) ) near the puncture?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta^* = \{ t \in \mathbb{C} : 0 < |t| < 1 \}$ be the punctured unit disk. The canonical line bundle $K_{\Delta^*}$ carries a canonical (singular) Hermitian metric $h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}$, defined as the supremum of all (semi-)positively curved Hermitian metrics on $K_{\Delta^*}$ with mass at most one, equivalently, the metric whose curvature current realizes the canonical $L^2$-extension/Bergman kernel construction on $\Delta^*$. Its inverse $h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1}$ is a (possibly singular) Hermitian metric on $K_{\Delta^*}^{-1}$, and may be viewed as a $(1,1)$-form (a section of $K_{\Delta^*}^{-1} \otimes \overline{K_{\Delta^*}^{-1}}$) on $\Delta^*$.

Prove or disprove: near the puncture $t = 0$, one has the asymptotic upper bound
$$
h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1} \;=\; O\!\left( \frac{\sqrt{-1}\, dt \wedge d\bar t}{|t|^2 (\log |t|)^2} \right),
$$
i.e., there exists a constant $C > 0$ and a neighborhood of $0$ in $\Delta^*$ on which
$$
h_{\mathrm{can},\Delta^*}^{-1} \;\le\; C \cdot \frac{\sqrt{-1}\, dt \wedge d\bar t}{|t|^2 (\log |t|)^2}.
$$

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety, let D be a divisor with only normal crossings such that K_X + D is ample, and set M := X \ D. Is the inverse supercanonical metric \hat h_{can,M}^{-1} on M a constant multiple of the Kähler–Einstein volume form on X constructed in the cited work [Ko]?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex projective variety and let $D \subset X$ be a reduced effective divisor with only simple normal crossings, such that the log canonical bundle $K_X + D$ is ample. Set $M := X \setminus D$.

Define the supercanonical Bergman-type Hermitian metric $\hat h_{\mathrm{can},M}$ on the canonical bundle $K_M$ as follows. For a holomorphic $n$-form $\sigma$ on $M$ (with $n = \dim X$) and a point $x \in M$, set
$$\hat h_{\mathrm{can},M}(\sigma,\sigma)(x)^{-1} \;=\; \sup\Bigl\{\,|f(x)|^2 \;:\; f\in H^0(M, K_M),\ \int_M (\sqrt{-1})^{n^2} f\wedge\bar f \le 1\,\Bigr\}^{-1}\cdot|\sigma(x)|^2,$$
so that $\hat h_{\mathrm{can},M}^{-1}$ is naturally a (possibly singular) volume form on $M$.

By the existence theorem for Kähler–Einstein metrics on log canonical pairs with $K_X+D$ ample, there is a unique Kähler–Einstein current $\omega_{KE}$ on $X$ with Ricci curvature $-\omega_{KE}$ on $M$ and Poincaré-type singularities along $D$; let $dV_{KE}$ denote its associated volume form on $M$.

Question: Is $\hat h_{\mathrm{can},M}^{-1}$ equal to a positive constant multiple of $dV_{KE}$ on $M$?
status_search_result: A literature search reveals extensive work on Kähler–Einstein metrics with mixed Poincaré/cone singularities along normal crossing divisors when $K_X+D$ is ample (existence and boundary asymptotics established by Guenancia, Berman–Guenancia, and others), but no source directly addressing whether the inverse supercanonical (Bergman-type) volume form on $M = X\setminus D$ coincides up to a constant with this Kähler–Einstein volume form was located. The status appears unknown.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let f: X → Y be a surjective proper projective morphism between complex manifolds, let D be a pseudoeffective Q-divisor on X, and let Y^o be the locus where f is smooth. If there exists y_0 in Y^o such that the divisor K_{X_{y_0}} + D_{y_0} on the fiber X_{y_0} is pseudoeffective, must the relative adjoint divisor K_{X/Y} + D be pseudoeffective on X?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f\colon X \to Y$ be a surjective proper projective morphism between complex manifolds, and let $D$ be a pseudoeffective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on $X$. Denote by $Y^o := \{y \in Y \mid f \text{ is smooth at every point of } X_y\}$ the smooth locus of $f$, and for $y \in Y^o$ write $X_y := f^{-1}(y)$ and $D_y := D|_{X_y}$. Let $K_{X/Y} := K_X - f^* K_Y$ be the relative canonical divisor.

A $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor on a complex manifold is called pseudoeffective if its first Chern class lies in the closure of the cone generated by classes of effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors (equivalently, it carries a singular Hermitian metric with semipositive curvature current).

Prove or disprove: if there exists a point $y_0 \in Y^o$ such that the $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $K_{X_{y_0}} + D_{y_0}$ on the fiber $X_{y_0}$ is pseudoeffective, then the relative adjoint $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $K_{X/Y} + D$ is pseudoeffective on $X$.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Let X be a compact Kähler manifold. If the canonical bundle K_X is not nef, must X contain a rational curve?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold, and let $K_X$ denote its canonical line bundle. Recall that a line bundle $L$ on $X$ is said to be nef if $\int_C c_1(L) \geq 0$ for every irreducible compact curve $C \subset X$. A rational curve on $X$ is a non-constant holomorphic image of $\mathbb{P}^1$ in $X$.

Prove or disprove: If $K_X$ is not nef, then $X$ contains a rational curve.

paper_title: Some Conjectures and Problems in Complex Geometry
original_question: Given a polarized manifold (X, L), what restrictions must its Hilbert polynomial P_{(X,L)}(m) = χ(X, O_X(mL)) satisfy?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, L)$ be a polarized manifold, that is, a smooth complex projective variety $X$ together with an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. Define the Hilbert polynomial of $(X,L)$ by
$$P_{(X,L)}(m) = \chi(X, \mathcal{O}_X(mL)) = \sum_{i=0}^{\dim X} (-1)^i \dim_{\mathbb{C}} H^i(X, \mathcal{O}_X(mL)),$$
which is a polynomial in $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ of degree $n = \dim X$ with rational coefficients.

Determine nontrivial restrictions that must be satisfied by such a Hilbert polynomial. More precisely, characterize (or give necessary conditions on) the set of polynomials $P(m) \in \mathbb{Q}[m]$ that can arise as $P_{(X,L)}(m)$ for some polarized manifold $(X,L)$, beyond the obvious requirements that $\deg P = n$, that $P$ takes integer values on $\mathbb{Z}$, and that the leading coefficient $L^n/n!$ is positive.
status_search_result: This is posed as an open-ended research problem asking for any restrictions on Hilbert polynomials of polarized manifolds. While certain special results are known (e.g., Fujita's classification in low degrees, positivity of the leading coefficient, integer-valuedness, and constraints from Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch involving Todd classes), no complete characterization of admissible Hilbert polynomials is known, and the problem is generally regarded as widely open.
