original_question: Letp be a prime, G a finite group with Op(G) = 1 , and B a p-block of G which is not of defect 0. Then ∑ C∈R(G)/G (-1)|C|k(C,B,d ) = 0.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and $G$ a finite group. Denote by $O_p(G)$ the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $G$, and assume $O_p(G)=1$. Let $B$ be a $p$-block of $G$ which is not of defect $0$.

Let $\mathcal{R}(G)$ denote the set of all strictly increasing chains
$$C: \ 1 = P_0 < P_1 < \cdots < P_{|C|}$$
of $p$-subgroups of $G$ starting at the trivial subgroup, where $|C|$ denotes the length of the chain. The group $G$ acts on $\mathcal{R}(G)$ by simultaneous conjugation on all members of a chain; let $\mathcal{R}(G)/G$ denote the set of $G$-orbits. For a chain $C \in \mathcal{R}(G)$, let $G_C = \bigcap_{i=0}^{|C|} N_G(P_i)$ denote its stabilizer.

For a non-negative integer $d$, let $k(G_C, B, d)$ denote the number of irreducible complex characters of $G_C$ of $p$-defect $d$ that lie in some $p$-block $b$ of $G_C$ whose induced (Brauer) block $b^G$ equals $B$.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $d \ge 0$,
$$\sum_{C \in \mathcal{R}(G)/G} (-1)^{|C|}\, k(G_C, B, d) \;=\; 0.$$
category_tag: Modular representation theory of finite groups
status_search_result: The statement is the Knörr–Robinson reformulation of Alperin's weight conjecture in its block-and-defect form. Alperin's weight conjecture (and equivalently this alternating-sum identity over G-orbits of p-chains) remains open in general; only special cases (specific families of groups, certain defect groups, small primes) have been verified. Recent work (e.g. functorial-equivalence and Galois-equivariant refinements posted as recently as 2025) continues to treat it as an open conjecture.

paper_title: Guido’s Book of Conjectures: A Gift to Guido Mislin on the Occasion of His Retirement from ETHZ, June 2006
original_question: LetF be a fusion system on P and P ′a strongly F-closed subgroup of P . Then there exists a normal fusion subsystem F ′ofF on P ′.
self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime and $P$ a finite $p$-group. A fusion system $\mathcal{F}$ on $P$ is a category whose objects are the subgroups of $P$ and whose morphisms are injective group homomorphisms which include all those induced by conjugation in $P$, subject to the standard axioms (every morphism factors as an isomorphism in $\mathcal{F}$ followed by an inclusion, and $\mathrm{Hom}_P(Q,R) \subseteq \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{F}}(Q,R)$ for all $Q,R \le P$). Assume $\mathcal{F}$ is saturated in the usual sense.

A subgroup $P' \le P$ is called strongly $\mathcal{F}$-closed if for every $Q \le P'$ and every morphism $\varphi \in \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal{F}}(Q,P)$ one has $\varphi(Q) \le P'$.

A saturated fusion subsystem $\mathcal{F}'$ of $\mathcal{F}$ on $P'$ is called normal if it is invariant under $\mathcal{F}$ in the appropriate sense (e.g. $P'$ is strongly $\mathcal{F}$-closed, and $\mathcal{F}'$ is stable under $\mathcal{F}$-conjugation of subgroups and morphisms, with the Frattini-type extension property of normal subsystems).

Prove or disprove: for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal{F}$ on a finite $p$-group $P$ and every strongly $\mathcal{F}$-closed subgroup $P' \le P$, there exists a normal fusion subsystem $\mathcal{F}'$ of $\mathcal{F}$ on $P'$.
status_search_result: Subsequent work on the local theory of fusion systems (notably by Craven and others) shows that the conjecture is false for strongly normal subsystems in general: there exist saturated (even constrained) fusion systems $\mathcal{F}$ with a strongly $\mathcal{F}$-closed subgroup admitting no normal subsystem on it. For the weaker notion of weakly normal subsystems, related affirmative results exist but the general question (depending on the choice of definition of "normal") is not fully settled and the conjecture as originally stated does not hold in the strong-normal form.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Local rigidity for split Cartan subgroup actions
original_question: Let G be a connected semisimple Lie group, Γ an irreducible lattice in G, and A a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup of G with dim A > 1. Is every C^1-small perturbation of the action of A on G/Γ C^∞-conjugate to an action of A defined by a continuous homomorphism from A to the centralizer of A in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group, let $\Gamma$ be an irreducible lattice in $G$, and let $A$ be a closed subgroup of a split Cartan subgroup of $G$ with $\dim A > 1$. The group $A$ acts on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$ by left translations. 

Prove or disprove the following: every $C^1$-small perturbation of the $A$-action on $G/\Gamma$ is $C^\infty$-conjugate to an action of $A$ on $G/\Gamma$ defined by left translation through a continuous homomorphism from $A$ into the centralizer $Z_G(A)$ of $A$ in $G$.

Here, two smooth $A$-actions $\alpha, \beta$ on $G/\Gamma$ are said to be $C^\infty$-conjugate if there exists a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $h: G/\Gamma \to G/\Gamma$ such that $h \circ \alpha(a) = \beta(a) \circ h$ for all $a \in A$. A $C^1$-small perturbation refers to a smooth $A$-action whose generators are close to those of the original action in the $C^1$ topology.
category_tag: Local rigidity of higher-rank abelian actions
status_search_result: The conjecture (a Katok–Spatzier style local rigidity statement) is known in several important cases — notably when $A$ is the full split Cartan subgroup or, more generally, when $A$ is not contained in a wall of a Weyl chamber — and recent work has established centralizer/local rigidity near generic elements of the Weyl chamber flow. The general case (in particular when $A$ lies in a Weyl chamber wall, with $\dim A > 1$) remains open.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
original_question: Is every Anosov diffeomorphism topologically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism on an infranilmanifold?
self_contained_problem:
A diffeomorphism f: M → M of a smooth closed Riemannian manifold M is called Anosov if there exist a continuous Df-invariant splitting of the tangent bundle TM = E^s ⊕ E^u and constants C > 0, 0 < λ < 1 such that for all n ≥ 0,
  ‖Df^n(v)‖ ≤ C λ^n ‖v‖ for v ∈ E^s,  and  ‖Df^{-n}(v)‖ ≤ C λ^n ‖v‖ for v ∈ E^u.
An infranilmanifold is a quotient Γ\N of a simply connected nilpotent Lie group N by a torsion-free discrete subgroup Γ of N ⋊ K, where K is a compact subgroup of Aut(N), such that Γ ∩ N has finite index in Γ. A hyperbolic automorphism of an infranilmanifold is a diffeomorphism induced by an automorphism A ∈ Aut(N) that preserves Γ and whose differential at the identity has no eigenvalue of absolute value 1.

Question: Is it true that every Anosov diffeomorphism (on any smooth closed manifold) is topologically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of an infranilmanifold? That is, for every Anosov f: M → M, do there exist an infranilmanifold Γ\N, a hyperbolic automorphism A of Γ\N, and a homeomorphism h: M → Γ\N such that h ∘ f = A ∘ h?
status_search_result: This is the well-known classification conjecture for Anosov diffeomorphisms (often attributed to Anosov and Smale). It remains open in general; the only known examples of Anosov diffeomorphisms are (up to topological conjugacy) hyperbolic automorphisms of infranilmanifolds, and the conjecture has been verified in special cases such as codimension-one Anosov diffeomorphisms and Anosov diffeomorphisms already living on infranilmanifolds, but the general case is unresolved.

context_brief: Global rigidity of irreducible higher-rank Anosov actions
original_question: Is every irreducible Anosov action of Z^k or R^k, with k ≥ 2, C^∞-conjugate to an algebraic action?
self_contained_problem:
Let $k\geq 2$ and let $G$ be either $\mathbb{Z}^k$ or $\mathbb{R}^k$. A smooth action $\alpha:G\times M\to M$ on a closed connected smooth manifold $M$ is called an Anosov action if there exists some $g\in G$ such that $\alpha(g,\cdot):M\to M$ is an Anosov diffeomorphism (in the $\mathbb{Z}^k$ case) or such that the time-one map of the flow generated by $g$ is normally hyperbolic to the $G$-orbit foliation (in the $\mathbb{R}^k$ case). An algebraic action is one of the following model type: $M=H/\Lambda$ where $H$ is a simply connected Lie group and $\Lambda\leq H$ is a cocompact lattice (or more generally a compact quotient of a Lie group by a closed subgroup), and $G$ acts by automorphisms of $H$ preserving $\Lambda$ and by left translations. original_question: Is every action of a connected semisimple Lie group whose simple factors all have real rank at least 2, or of a lattice in such a group, that contains an element acting nontrivially and uniformly partially hyperbolically C^∞-conjugate to an algebraic action?
self_contained_problem:

with at least one of $E^s$, $E^u$ nontrivial (so that $f$ acts nontrivially). An action is called algebraic if it is built, up to finite covers, from translations on quotients of Lie groups by lattices and from affine actions on infranilmanifolds.

original_question: Do measure-rigidity results for higher-rank abelian group actions produce obstructions to smooth or continuous irreducible actions of a higher-rank abelian group on a compact manifold?
self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a higher-rank abelian group (for example $\mathbb{Z}^k$ or $\mathbb{R}^k$ with $k \geq 2$). An action of $A$ on a compact manifold $M$ is called irreducible if it admits no nontrivial invariant smooth foliation or, equivalently, no rank-one subaction preserves a measurable splitting into invariant sub-bundles (so that the action genuinely uses its higher-rank structure). 

Recent measure-rigidity theorems assert, under suitable hyperbolicity hypotheses, that every invariant Borel probability measure for such an action is of an algebraic type (e.g. Haar measure on a homogeneous subspace, or a measure with positive entropy must be absolutely continuous).

Question: Do these measure-rigidity results for higher-rank abelian group actions yield obstructions to the existence of irreducible smooth (or merely continuous) actions of a higher-rank abelian group on a given compact manifold $M$? Concretely, determine compact manifolds $M$ on which no irreducible smooth (resp. continuous) action of a higher-rank abelian group $A$ can exist, with the nonexistence deduced from measure-rigidity phenomena.
category_tag: Measure rigidity of abelian group actions
status_search_result: The question, attributed to D. Fisher and appearing in workshop problem lists on measure rigidity, is reported in problem collections (e.g., AIM workshop "Emerging Applications of Measure Rigidity") and remains a guiding open question. While there has been substantial progress on measure rigidity for higher-rank abelian and lattice actions (Katok–Spatzier, Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss, and more recent work by Brown–Fisher–Hurtado, Rodriguez Hertz–Wang), no resolution producing definitive topological/smooth obstructions to irreducible higher-rank abelian actions on compact manifolds in the generality posed has been identified. paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Furstenberg measure rigidity on the circle
original_question: For multiplicatively independent positive integers m and n, are the only probability Borel measures on R/Z that are ergodic under the semigroup generated by multiplication by m and multiplication by n the Lebesgue measure and finite-support measures?
self_contained_problem:
Let $m$ and $n$ be multiplicatively independent positive integers (i.e., there are no positive integers $a,b$ with $m^a = n^b$). Consider the semigroup $S_{m,n}$ of continuous self-maps of the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ generated by the two maps $T_m(x) = mx \bmod 1$ and $T_n(x) = nx \bmod 1$. A Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ is said to be $S_{m,n}$-invariant if $(T_m)_*\mu = \mu$ and $(T_n)_*\mu = \mu$, and $S_{m,n}$-ergodic if every Borel set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ with $T_m^{-1}(A) = A$ and $T_n^{-1}(A) = A$ satisfies $\mu(A) \in \{0,1\}$. 

Prove or disprove: the only $S_{m,n}$-ergodic Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ are the Lebesgue (Haar) measure and the measures supported on finite sets (equivalently, on finite $S_{m,n}$-invariant subsets of $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, which consist of rational points).
status_search_result: This is Furstenberg's well-known ×m, ×n measure rigidity conjecture. It remains open in general. Rudolph (1990) and Johnson proved it under the additional assumption of positive entropy with respect to one of the maps, but the zero-entropy case is still unresolved.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
original_question: For an algebraic Anosov action of R^k or Z^k, k ≥ 2, on a biquotient M of a connected Lie group G, and for an ergodic probability Borel measure μ on M, must either μ be a finite sum of measures constructed from Haar measures on closed subgroups of G, or must supp μ fiber equivariantly over a manifold N on which the action reduces to rank one?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group and let $M = \Gamma_1 \backslash G / \Gamma_2$ be a biquotient of $G$ (a manifold obtained as the quotient of $G$ by a free, properly discontinuous two-sided action of discrete subgroups). An action of $\mathbb{R}^k$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k$ on $M$ is called algebraic if it is induced by left translations on $G$ by elements of a subgroup commuting with the relevant structure, and it is called Anosov if some element of the acting group acts as an Anosov diffeomorphism (or flow). Fix $k \geq 2$ and an algebraic Anosov action of $\mathbb{R}^k$ or $\mathbb{Z}^k$ on $M$. Let $\mu$ be an ergodic probability Borel measure on $M$ invariant under this action. 

Prove or disprove: at least one of the following must hold.
(i) $\mu$ is a finite sum of measures each of which is constructed from a Haar measure supported on a closed subgroup of $G$ (i.e., the push-forward to $M$ of a translate of such a Haar measure).
(ii) The support of $\mu$ fibers equivariantly over a manifold $N$ in such a way that the induced action on $N$ reduces to a rank-one action.

status_search_result: The Katok–Spatzier measure rigidity conjecture for algebraic Anosov actions of higher-rank abelian groups remains open in full generality. original_question: Suppose H acts on a space X preserving a geometric structure, and P is a parabolic subgroup in the ambient setting. Under what conditions on X is every finite P-invariant measure H-invariant; equivalently, which H-actions are stiff?
self_contained_problem:
Let G be a real Lie group and let P ≤ G be a parabolic subgroup. Let H be a subgroup of G (or, more generally, a locally compact group together with a fixed homomorphism into G whose image generates a parabolic-relevant subgroup) and suppose H acts on a topological space X preserving a prescribed geometric structure (for example, a smooth structure, a homogeneous structure of the form X = G/Γ for a discrete subgroup Γ ≤ G with H acting by left translation, an affine structure, or a Riemannian metric). A finite Borel measure μ on X is called P-invariant if it is preserved by every element of P acting on X (when such an action is defined on X via the ambient G-action), and H-invariant if it is preserved by every element of H. The H-action on X is called stiff if every finite P-invariant Borel probability measure on X is automatically H-invariant.

Problem. Determine geometric/dynamical conditions on the space X (and on the action of H and the parabolic subgroup P) under which every finite P-invariant Borel probability measure on X is H-invariant. Equivalently, characterize the class of H-actions on such spaces X that are stiff.
status_search_result: Stiffness questions of this general type (attributed to Lindenstrauss/Furstenberg-style measure rigidity) remain an active research area. context_brief: Horospherical Radon measures in rank one
original_question: For a noncompact semisimple Lie group G of rank one, a discrete subgroup Γ of G, and a horospherical subgroup U of G, what are the U-ergodic Radon measures on G/Γ? In particular, are they all either carried by closed U-orbits or obtained from the harmonic-function construction?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a noncompact semisimple Lie group of real rank one, let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a discrete subgroup (not necessarily a lattice), and let $U \subset G$ be a horospherical subgroup (i.e., the unipotent radical of a minimal parabolic subgroup of $G$). Consider the action of $U$ on the homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$ by left translation. A Radon measure on $G/\Gamma$ is a Borel measure that is finite on compact sets, and such a measure is called $U$-ergodic if it is $U$-invariant and every $U$-invariant Borel set has either zero or full measure on every $U$-invariant Borel set of finite measure (in the locally finite sense).

Two standard families of $U$-ergodic Radon measures on $G/\Gamma$ are known:
(i) measures supported on a single closed $U$-orbit in $G/\Gamma$;
(ii) measures arising from the "harmonic function construction," namely measures associated to positive eigenfunctions (with respect to the appropriate Laplace–Beltrami operator) of the geodesic flow / boundary measures, generalizing the Babillot–Ledrappier construction on hyperbolic surfaces.

Question: Classify all $U$-ergodic Radon measures on $G/\Gamma$. In particular, is every such measure either supported on a closed $U$-orbit or obtained from the harmonic function construction?

status_search_result: The problem is broadly open in full generality, but substantial partial results exist. However, the complete classification on arbitrary discrete subgroups Γ of a rank-one Lie group G remains open.

original_question: If Γ is a normal conilpotent subgroup of a uniform lattice in SL(2,R), is the Haar measure nonsquashable, meaning that the centralizer of the horocycle flow does not contain an invertible nonsingular transformation that fails to preserve the measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and let $\Lambda \subset G$ be a uniform (cocompact) lattice. Let $\Gamma \trianglelefteq \Lambda$ be a normal subgroup such that the quotient $\Lambda/\Gamma$ is conilpotent (i.e., a finitely generated nilpotent group). Consider the homogeneous space $X = \Gamma \backslash G$ equipped with the right action of the one-parameter unipotent (horocycle) subgroup
$$u_t = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & t \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad t \in \mathbb{R},$$
and let $\mu$ denote the (infinite, in general) Haar measure on $X$ induced from Haar measure on $G$.

A $u_t$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on $X$ is called squashable if the centralizer of the horocycle flow $\{u_t\}$ (in the group of invertible nonsingular transformations of $(X,\mu)$) contains an invertible nonsingular transformation that does not preserve $\mu$; otherwise $\mu$ is called nonsquashable.

Question: Is the Haar measure $\mu$ on $X = \Gamma \backslash G$ nonsquashable?

original_question: For an Anosov flow on a compact Riemannian manifold whose stable bundle has an invariant splitting and fast stable foliation W^s_+, what are the invariant ergodic measures for W^s_+?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi_t : M \to M$ be a $C^\infty$ Anosov flow on a compact Riemannian manifold $M$, with hyperbolic splitting $TM = E^s \oplus E^0 \oplus E^u$, where $E^0$ is the line spanned by the generator of the flow, and $E^s$, $E^u$ are the stable and unstable bundles. Assume that the stable bundle admits a $D\phi_t$-invariant continuous splitting
$$E^s = E^s_+ \oplus E^s_-,$$
into "fast" and "slow" sub-bundles, with the property that vectors in $E^s_+$ are contracted strictly faster than vectors in $E^s_-$ under the forward flow. Assume that the fast sub-bundle $E^s_+$ is integrable, and let $W^s_+$ be the corresponding "fast stable" foliation of $M$, whose leaves are smooth submanifolds tangent to $E^s_+$.

A Radon measure $\mu$ on $M$ is called invariant for the foliation $W^s_+$ if its conditional measures on the leaves of $W^s_+$ are (almost everywhere) given by the Riemannian volume on the leaves up to a constant, equivalently if $\mu$ is invariant under all holonomy-respecting translations along $W^s_+$. Such a measure $\mu$ is ergodic for $W^s_+$ if every $W^s_+$-saturated Borel set has either zero or full $\mu$-measure.

Problem: Describe (i.e., classify) all locally finite Borel measures on $M$ that are invariant and ergodic for the fast stable foliation $W^s_+$.
category_tag: Invariant measures for foliations of Anosov flows
status_search_result: The question, posed as a nonlinear analog of Ratner's/Raghunathan's measure classification for unipotent flows, remains open in general. Partial results exist: Babillot–Ledrappier classified invariant measures for the strong stable (horocyclic) foliation on abelian covers of compact negatively curved surfaces, and later work has extended ergodicity and unique quasi-ergodicity results to broader settings (e.g., Anosov flows with Hölder potentials, hyperbolic equilibrium states). No complete classification for the fast stable foliation of a general Anosov flow with invariant stable splitting is known.

original_question: Let G be a Lie group, Γ a lattice in G, U={u(t)} a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup, and x∈G/Γ with dense Ux. Can one prove equidistribution in G/Γ of {u(t_n)x} when t_n is [n^α] for α>1, [P(n)] for a polynomial P, or the nth prime number?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma\subset G$ a lattice, and $\pi:G\to G/\Gamma$ the natural projection. Let $U=\{u(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ be a one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroup of $G$ (i.e., $\mathrm{Ad}(u(t))$ is a unipotent linear operator for every $t$). Fix a point $x\in G/\Gamma$ whose orbit $Ux=\{u(t)x:t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ is dense in $G/\Gamma$. By Ratner's theorem, this implies that the orbit is equidistributed with respect to the $G$-invariant probability measure $\mu_{G/\Gamma}$, i.e., $\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T f(u(t)x)\,dt \to \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu_{G/\Gamma}$ for all $f\in C_c(G/\Gamma)$.

For each of the following sequences $(t_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of real numbers, determine whether the discrete orbit $\{u(t_n)x\}_{n\ge 1}$ is equidistributed in $G/\Gamma$ with respect to $\mu_{G/\Gamma}$, in the sense that for every $f\in C_c(G/\Gamma)$,
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N f(u(t_n)x) \longrightarrow \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu_{G/\Gamma} \quad\text{as } N\to\infty.$$

(1) $t_n = \lfloor n^\alpha\rfloor$ for a fixed real $\alpha>1$.

(2) $t_n = \lfloor P(n)\rfloor$ for a fixed polynomial $P\in\mathbb{R}[x]$ of degree $\ge 1$.

(3) $t_n = p_n$, the $n$-th prime number.
status_search_result: The problem is known in various special cases (horocycle flows on $SL_2(\mathbb{R})/\Gamma$ along polynomial and prime times, and on nilmanifolds by Green–Tao), and recent works (e.g., Lindenstrauss–Mohammadi–Wang and others on effective equidistribution; Sarnak–Ubis on horocycle at primes; sparse equidistribution results 2018–2024) provide partial progress, but the general Margulis question for arbitrary Lie groups, lattices, and one-parameter Ad-unipotent subgroups along these sparse sequences remains open.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
original_question: Let V be a connected Ad-unipotent subgroup of a Lie group G, Γ a lattice in G, and x∈G/Γ with dense Vx. For a good sequence of subsets A_n⊂V and every f∈C_c(G/Γ), do the normalized Haar averages of f(vx) over A_n converge to the Haar probability integral on G/Γ with an effective error term?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected Lie group, $\Gamma \subset G$ a lattice, and let $\mu$ denote the $G$-invariant Haar probability measure on $G/\Gamma$. Let $V \subset G$ be a connected Ad-unipotent subgroup (i.e., for every $v\in V$, the adjoint operator $\mathrm{Ad}(v)$ on the Lie algebra of $G$ is unipotent), and equip $V$ with a Haar measure $dv$. Fix a point $x\in G/\Gamma$ such that the orbit $Vx$ is dense in $G/\Gamma$.

By Ratner's theorem (with Shah's extension), for a suitably "good" increasing sequence of bounded measurable subsets $A_n \subset V$ (for instance, a Følner sequence of well-rounded balls with respect to a suitable norm on $V$), and for every $f\in C_c(G/\Gamma)$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\mathrm{Vol}(A_n)} \int_{A_n} f(vx)\,dv \;=\; \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu.$$

Prove that this convergence holds with an effective error term: that is, find an explicit function $\varepsilon(n)\to 0$ (e.g., a polynomial rate $\mathrm{Vol}(A_n)^{-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$, depending on Sobolev norms of $f$, on $x$, and on the geometry of $A_n$) such that
$$\left| \frac{1}{\mathrm{Vol}(A_n)} \int_{A_n} f(vx)\,dv - \int_{G/\Gamma} f\,d\mu \right| \;\le\; \varepsilon(n)$$
for all $n$ and all $f\in C_c^\infty(G/\Gamma)$ (with the implied constants depending on $f$ through a Sobolev norm).
status_search_result: The problem in full generality (arbitrary connected Ad-unipotent subgroup V in arbitrary G/Γ) remains open and is widely regarded as a central challenge in homogeneous dynamics. Substantial recent progress has been made in specific settings: polynomial-rate effective equidistribution for one-parameter unipotent flows has been established in arithmetic quotients of SL₂(ℂ) and SL₂(ℝ)×SL₂(ℝ) by Lindenstrauss–Mohammadi (and Lindenstrauss–Mohammadi–Wang), and effective versions of Ratner/Shah-type equidistribution with polynomial rate have been obtained for products of SL₂ factors. These results do not yet cover the general unipotent case posed by Margulis.

original_question: Let L be a Lie group, G a closed subgroup, Λ a lattice in L, a∈G semisimple with expanding horospherical subgroup U, x0∈L/Λ with dense Gx0, γ:[0,1]→U analytic, and ν the pushforward of Lebesgue measure under t↦γ(t)x0. What condition on γ ensures that a^nν converges to Haar measure λ on L/Λ as n→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $L$ be a real Lie group and $G\subseteq L$ a closed subgroup. Let $\Lambda\subset L$ be a lattice, and consider the homogeneous space $L/\Lambda$ equipped with its $L$-invariant probability measure $\lambda$ (Haar measure). Let $a\in G$ be a semisimple element, and let
$$U=\{u\in G:\ a^{-n}ua^{n}\to e\text{ as }n\to\infty\}$$
be its expanding horospherical subgroup. Fix a point $x_0\in L/\Lambda$ whose $G$-orbit $Gx_0$ is dense in $L/\Lambda$. Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ be a real-analytic curve, and let $\nu$ be the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$ under the map $t\mapsto \gamma(t)\,x_0$, viewed as a probability measure on $L/\Lambda$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $\gamma$ under which the translates $a^{n}_{*}\nu$ converge weakly to $\lambda$ as $n\to\infty$.
status_search_result: The question (attributed to N. Shah) has been resolved in many important cases: when $\gamma$ is analytic and not contained in any proper subgroup of an appropriate subgroup of $G$, Shah and subsequent authors established equidistribution. The analyticity assumption has been weakened in low-rank settings (e.g., work of Shah–Yang, Solan–Wieser, and recent 2025 work on products of $\mathrm{SO}(n,1)$ factors). A complete characterization in full generality is not yet established, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Shah curve equidistribution for larger Lie groups
original_question: Does Shah's equidistribution result for L=SO(m,1) and G=SO(n,1), m>n, hold for all Lie groups L containing G=SO(n,1)?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let n ≥ 2 and let G = SO(n,1) denote the special orthogonal group of a real quadratic form of signature (n,1). Let L be a connected real Lie group containing G as a closed subgroup, let Γ ⊂ L be a lattice, and consider the finite-volume homogeneous space L/Γ on which G acts by left translations. Fix a one-parameter diagonal (R-split) subgroup {a_t : t ∈ R} of G whose adjoint action expands a unipotent subgroup U ⊂ G.

Let φ : I → G be an analytic (or smooth, nondegenerate) curve defined on a compact interval I ⊂ R, lying in the expanding horospherical subgroup associated with {a_t}, and assume φ does not lie in any proper subgroup obstructing equidistribution (i.e., φ is "generic" in the sense required by Shah's theorem). For x ∈ L/Γ let μ_t be the pushforward to L/Γ of normalized Lebesgue measure on I under s ↦ a_t φ(s) x.

Known result. When L = SO(m,1) with m > n, Shah proved that for every x ∈ L/Γ whose G-orbit closure is a homogeneous subset H·x (for some closed subgroup H with G ⊂ H ⊂ L admitting a finite H-invariant measure on H·x/Γ_H), the measures μ_t converge as t → ∞ in the weak-* topology to the unique H-invariant probability measure on H·x.

Question. Does the same equidistribution statement hold for every connected Lie group L containing G = SO(n,1)? Precisely: for any such L, any lattice Γ ⊂ L, any x ∈ L/Γ, and any sufficiently generic analytic curve φ as above, do the measures μ_t converge weak-* as t → ∞ to the algebraic probability measure supported on the orbit closure of x under the smallest closed subgroup H, G ⊂ H ⊂ L, such that H·x is closed and supports a finite H-invariant measure?
status_search_result: The conjecture has been established in additional cases beyond L = SO(m,1). In particular, Yang (2013/2016) proved the equidistribution in T^1(H^n) and related homogeneous spaces, and Shi–Yang and subsequent works (2017, 2022, and 2025) extended Shah's equidistribution result to the case when G is a product (SO(n_1,1) × ⋯ × SO(n_k,1)) acting on L/Γ. A statement valid for arbitrary connected Lie groups L containing SO(n,1) does not appear to have been established in full generality, so the conjecture is partially solved.

original_question: For a semisimple Lie group G acting on a real normed vector space V, a point p∈V with finite stabilizer, R_T={g∈G: ||gp||<T}, a lattice Γ in G, and μ_T the projection to G/Γ of normalized Haar measure on R_T, what is the limiting distribution of μ_T as T→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a connected semisimple real Lie group acting linearly on a finite-dimensional real normed vector space $(V, \|\cdot\|)$. Fix a point $p \in V$ whose stabilizer $G_p = \{g \in G : gp = p\}$ in $G$ is finite. For $T > 0$, define the "representation ball"
$$R_T = \{g \in G : \|gp\| < T\} \subset G,$$
and let $\nu_T$ denote the normalized Haar measure on $R_T$ (i.e., the restriction of a Haar measure on $G$ to $R_T$, rescaled to be a probability measure). Let $\Gamma \subset G$ be a lattice, and let $\pi : G \to G/\Gamma$ be the natural projection. Define the probability measure
$$\mu_T = \pi_* \nu_T$$
on $G/\Gamma$. Determine the limiting distribution (weak-$*$ limit as a probability measure on $G/\Gamma$) of $\mu_T$ as $T \to \infty$.
status_search_result: Significant partial results are known. Eskin–Mozes–Shah and Eskin–McMullen established equidistribution of translates of homogeneous measures in many cases, and Gorodnik–Weiss and Gorodnik–Oh proved equidistribution of dense lattice orbits on homogeneous varieties under suitable hypotheses. Recent finitary refinements (e.g., 2024 work on quantitative distribution of lattice orbits) continue to extend the picture, but a fully general answer for arbitrary semisimple G, V, p with finite stabilizer remains the subject of ongoing research.

context_brief: Pair correlations for quadratic Kronecker sequences
original_question: If α∈R is badly approximable by rationals, does the pair correlation R_2([a,b],N,α) for the sequence αn^2 mod 1 converge to b−a as N→∞?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $\alpha$ and an integer $N\ge 1$, let $\{\alpha n^2\}$ denote the fractional part of $\alpha n^2$ for $n=1,2,\dots,N$. For an interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$, define the pair correlation function
$$R_2([a,b],N,\alpha) \;=\; \frac{1}{N}\,\#\Bigl\{\,1\le m\ne n\le N \;:\; \{\alpha n^2\}-\{\alpha m^2\}\in \tfrac{1}{N}[a,b]+\mathbb{Z}\,\Bigr\}.$$
A real number $\alpha$ is said to be badly approximable by rationals if there exists a constant $c=c(\alpha)>0$ such that $|\alpha-p/q|\ge c/q^2$ for every rational $p/q$ (equivalently, the partial quotients of the continued-fraction expansion of $\alpha$ are bounded), together with the further Diophantine condition that for every convergent $p/q$ to $\alpha$, the square-free part of $q$ is $q^{1+o(1)}$.

Question: If $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ is badly approximable by rationals in the above sense, does one have
$$R_2([a,b],N,\alpha)\longrightarrow b-a \qquad\text{as }N\to\infty$$
for every interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$?
category_tag: Pair correlation of polynomial sequences mod 1
status_search_result: The Rudnick–Sarnak conjecture asserts Poissonian pair correlations for $\{\alpha n^2\}$ for Diophantine/badly approximable $\alpha$. It is known to hold for almost every $\alpha$ in the sense of Lebesgue measure (Rudnick–Sarnak), and partial results exist along subsequences (Rudnick–Sarnak–Zaharescu, Heath-Brown, Truelsen, Marklof–Yesha), but no specific badly approximable $\alpha$ has been verified. The conjecture remains open.

context_brief: Discrete horocycle equidistribution at cusp scale
original_question: For a continuous function f on T^1(X) with the stated cusp growth condition, badly approximable α∈R, and 0<c1<c2, do the averages M^{-1}∑_{m=1}^M f(u_y(αm)) converge uniformly to the Liouville integral as M→∞ for c1M^{-2}≤y≤c2M^{-2}?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma = \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ acting on the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$, let $X = \Gamma\backslash \mathbb{H}$ be the modular surface, and let $T^1(X)$ denote its unit tangent bundle, identified with $\Gamma\backslash \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Let $\lambda$ denote the normalized Liouville measure on $T^1(X)$. For $y>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$ let
$$u_y(x) = \begin{pmatrix} y^{1/2} & xy^{-1/2}\\ 0 & y^{-1/2}\end{pmatrix} \in \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R}),$$
viewed as a point in $T^1(X)$ via the projection. Thus, for fixed $y$, the map $x\mapsto u_y(x)$ parametrizes the closed horocycle at height $y$.

Recall that $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ is called badly approximable by rationals if there exists $c>0$ such that $|\alpha - p/q| \ge c/q^2$ for all $p/q\in\mathbb{Q}$.

Let $f\colon T^1(X)\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and satisfy a moderate growth condition at the cusp of $X$ (specifically, $f(g)\ll \mathrm{ht}(g)^{1/2-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$, where $\mathrm{ht}$ denotes the maximal imaginary part of a $\Gamma$-translate of the basepoint).

Question: For every such $f$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ that is badly approximable by rationals, and every $0<c_1<c_2$, does the discrete horocycle average
$$\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M} f\bigl(u_y(\alpha m)\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_{T^1(X)} f \, d\lambda$$
hold uniformly for $y\in[c_1 M^{-2},\, c_2 M^{-2}]$ as $M\to\infty$?
status_search_result: Web searches indicate active research by Marklof, Strömbergsson, and others on equidistribution of discrete horocycle orbits and shrinking-target/cusp-scale equidistribution on the modular surface. Partial results exist for almost every $\alpha$ and for various scales, but no source verifying resolution of the specific cusp-scale ($y \asymp M^{-2}$) conjecture for badly approximable $\alpha$ was found. Status appears to remain open, but this could not be conclusively confirmed.

original_question: For a finite-volume Riemannian locally symmetric space X of noncompact type, what is the asymptotic number of compact flats in X with volume less than T as T→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X = \Gamma\backslash G/K$ be a finite-volume Riemannian locally symmetric space of noncompact type, where $G$ is a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center and no compact factors, $K\subset G$ is a maximal compact subgroup, and $\Gamma\subset G$ is a lattice. By a flat in $X$ one means the image in $X$ of a maximal totally geodesic flat subspace of $G/K$ (so its dimension equals the real rank $r$ of $G$). A flat is called compact if its image in $X$ is a compact submanifold, in which case it carries an induced Riemannian volume.

For $T>0$, let $N(T)$ denote the number of compact flats in $X$ whose $r$-dimensional volume is at most $T$. Determine the asymptotic behavior of $N(T)$ as $T\to\infty$.

context_brief: Divergent torus orbits in arithmetic quotients
original_question: Let G be a semisimple real algebraic group, Γ a noncocompact arithmetic lattice, and D a closed subgroup of a maximal R-split torus A. self_contained_problem:
Let G be a semisimple real algebraic group defined over Q, let Γ ⊂ G be a noncocompact (non-uniform) arithmetic lattice, and let A ⊂ G be a maximal R-split torus. Let D be a closed subgroup of A acting by left multiplication on the homogeneous space Γ\G. A trajectory {Γg·d : d ∈ D} is called divergent if the map D → Γ\G, d ↦ Γg d, is proper (i.e. it eventually leaves every compact set of Γ\G). A divergent D-trajectory through Γg is called obvious (algebraic) if there exists a Q-parabolic subgroup P of G and a Q-character χ of P such that g·D is contained in a coset on which |χ| tends to 0 (equivalently, the divergence is forced by the orbit eventually lying in a degenerating one-parameter family of Q-parabolic horospherical directions). Let r = rank_Q(G) denote the Q-rank of G. Prove or disprove the following three statements:

(1) If dim D > r, then there are no divergent D-orbits in Γ\G.

(2) If dim D = r, then every divergent D-trajectory is obvious.

(3) If dim D < r, then there exist non-obvious divergent D-trajectories.

status_search_result: Parts (1) and (2) of the conjecture have been resolved in the affirmative: recent work (e.g., "On Topologically Big Divergent Trajectories", arXiv:2201.04221) shows that when A has dimension ≥ rank_Q G, every divergent A-trajectory in Γ\G diverges for a purely algebraic reason, settling Weiss's long-standing conjecture in that regime. Part (3), asserting the existence of non-obvious divergent trajectories when dim D < rank_Q G, is established in various cases (e.g., Q-rank 2) but has not been fully verified in complete generality.

context_brief: Symbolic coding for Weyl chamber flow
original_question: Can analogs of geometric coding and arithmetic coding be constructed for the Weyl chamber flow, equivalently the diagonal group action, on SL(n,R)/SL(n,Z)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$, and consider the homogeneous space $X = \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$ equipped with the right action of the full positive diagonal subgroup
$$A = \{\mathrm{diag}(e^{t_1},\ldots,e^{t_n}) : t_i \in \mathbb{R},\ t_1+\cdots+t_n = 0\},$$
called the Weyl chamber flow.

For the geodesic flow on the modular surface $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ (the case $n=2$), there are two classical symbolic representations: 
(i) a "geometric coding" obtained from a fundamental domain by recording the sequence of sides crossed by an oriented geodesic (equivalently, oriented excursions into the cusp); and 
(ii) "arithmetic codings" obtained from continued fraction expansions via Gauss-type reduction theory, which yield (countable-alphabet) topological Markov shifts conjugate—on suitable invariant sets—to the geodesic flow.

Problem: For $n \geq 3$, construct analogs of both the geometric coding and the arithmetic coding for the Weyl chamber flow (the $A$-action) on $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{Z})$. That is, produce symbolic dynamical systems—ideally of a Markov or countable-Markov nature—obtained, respectively, from a geometric fundamental-domain construction and from a higher-dimensional arithmetic/continued-fraction-type reduction theory, together with maps that conjugate (or semiconjugate) them to the diagonal action on $X$.
status_search_result: The problem, attributed to S. Katok, appears in open-problem lists in dynamics. While geometric and arithmetic codings are well-developed for the rank-one geodesic flow on the modular surface (Katok, Ugarcovici, and others), and partial symbolic codings related to higher-rank diagonal actions have appeared (e.g., in work toward Littlewood's conjecture noted by B. Weiss), no satisfactory analog of both the geometric and arithmetic codings for the full Weyl chamber flow on SL(n,R)/SL(n,Z) for n ≥ 3 has been constructed. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Can one find a triangle whose angles are Diophantine modulo 2π and whose billiard flow is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure?

A real number $\alpha$ is called Diophantine modulo $2\pi$ if there exist constants $C>0$ and $s>0$ such that for every nonzero integer $n$, the distance from $n\alpha$ to the nearest integer multiple of $2\pi$ is at least $C|n|^{-s}$. Consider a triangle $T\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with interior angles $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$ (so $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=\pi$). The billiard flow on $T$ is the flow on the unit tangent bundle of $T$ given by straight-line motion with elastic reflection off the boundary (and undefined at the vertices). It preserves the Liouville measure (the product of Lebesgue area on $T$ with arc-length on the unit circle of directions).

original_question: Does there exist a weakly mixing polygonal billiard; in particular, are Vorobets' billiards weakly mixing?
self_contained_problem:
A polygonal billiard is the dynamical system obtained by letting a point particle move in straight lines inside a planar polygon $P$, reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equal to angle of reflection) at the boundary. The associated billiard flow acts on the unit tangent bundle of $P$ and preserves the Liouville measure. The flow is said to be weakly mixing (with respect to the Liouville measure) if the product flow on the product of the phase space with itself is ergodic, equivalently, if the Koopman operator has no non-constant measurable eigenfunctions.

Vorobets' billiards are a class of polygons constructed by Ya. B. Vorobets, defined as polygons whose angles can be approximated very rapidly by rationals (a super-Liouville condition), in such a way that ergodicity of the billiard flow is guaranteed.

Questions:
(a) Does there exist a polygon $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ whose billiard flow is weakly mixing with respect to the Liouville measure?
(b) In particular, are the billiards in Vorobets' polygons weakly mixing?
status_search_result: Chaika and Forni (arXiv:2003.00890, "Weakly Mixing Polygonal Billiards") proved that there exists a residual (Baire generic) set of polygons whose billiard flow is weakly mixing with respect to the Liouville measure, thus answering the existence question (a) positively. The specific question (b), whether Vorobets' billiards themselves are weakly mixing, does not appear to be fully resolved by this generic result.

original_question: Let G be the direct product of k≥2 copies of SL(2,R), let U+ and U− be the upper and lower unipotent subgroups, and let Γ+ and Γ− be irreducible lattices in U+ and U−. If the group generated by Γ+ and Γ− is discrete, is it an arithmetic lattice in G?
self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 2 be an integer and let G = SL(2, ℝ)^k. Inside SL(2, ℝ), let

  U = { ( 1 x ; 0 1 ) : x ∈ ℝ },   U⁻ = { ( 1 0 ; y 1 ) : y ∈ ℝ }

denote the upper and lower unipotent subgroups, and define the upper and lower unipotent subgroups of G by

  U₊ = U × U × ⋯ × U  (k factors),   U₋ = U⁻ × U⁻ × ⋯ × U⁻  (k factors).

A lattice Γ in U₊ (which is isomorphic as a Lie group to ℝ^k) is called irreducible if it is not commensurable to a direct product of lattices coming from any nontrivial partition of the k factors; equivalently, Γ does not split as Γ₁ × Γ₂ under any decomposition U₊ = U^{S} × U^{S'} with S ⊔ S' = {1,…,k} a nontrivial partition. Irreducibility of a lattice Γ in U₋ is defined analogously.

Let Γ₊ ⊂ U₊ and Γ₋ ⊂ U₋ be irreducible lattices, and let ⟨Γ₊, Γ₋⟩ ⊆ G denote the subgroup of G generated by Γ₊ ∪ Γ₋.

Question: If ⟨Γ₊, Γ₋⟩ is a discrete subgroup of G, must it be an arithmetic lattice in G?

status_search_result: Y. Benoist and S. Miquel (Duke Math. J. 169 (2020), no. 8; preprint arXiv:1805.00045, 2018) proved that for any semisimple real algebraic Lie group G of real rank at least 2, any discrete Zariski-dense subgroup of G that contains an irreducible lattice of the unipotent radical of a nontrivial parabolic subgroup is an arithmetic lattice of G. This resolves the Margulis–Selberg conjecture, of which the stated question (for G = SL(2,ℝ)^k with k ≥ 2 and Γ₊, Γ₋ irreducible lattices in opposite unipotent subgroups generating a discrete group, which is automatically Zariski dense) is a special case. paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Nondegenerate matrix-valued maps and VWA avoidance
original_question: Can one find reasonable and checkable conditions for a smooth map f:U⊂R^k→M_{m×n}(R) that generalize nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and imply that almost every point of f(U) is not very well approximable?
self_contained_problem:
Let $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the space of real $m\times n$ matrices. A matrix $Y\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ is called very well approximable (VWA) if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the inequality
$$\|Y\mathbf{q}-\mathbf{p}\|^m \,\|\mathbf{q}\|^{n} < \|\mathbf{q}\|^{-\varepsilon}$$
has infinitely many solutions $(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q})\in\mathbb{Z}^m\times(\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\})$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes a fixed norm. For vector-valued smooth maps $f:U\subset\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}^n$, recall that $f$ is called nondegenerate at $x_0\in U$ if the partial derivatives of $f$ at $x_0$ of orders up to some $\ell$ span $\mathbb{R}^n$; it is known that nondegeneracy of $f$ at almost every point implies that almost every point of $f(U)$ is not VWA.
 
Problem: Formulate reasonable and effectively checkable conditions on a smooth map
$$f:U\subset\mathbb{R}^k\longrightarrow M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$$
that generalize the notion of nondegeneracy from the vector-valued case ($m=1$) and that imply: with respect to Lebesgue measure on $U$, almost every point of the image $f(U)$ is not very well approximable.
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on Diophantine approximation for matrix-valued maps: Kleinbock–Margulis–Wang, Beresnevich–Kleinbock–Margulis, Aka–Breuillard–Rosenzweig–de Saxcé and others have proven extremality for various classes (e.g., the matrix Veronese curve, analytic submanifolds satisfying constraint conditions). However, a fully general and "checkable" notion of nondegeneracy for smooth matrix-valued maps yielding non-VWA almost everywhere is not yet established in the same clean form as the vector-valued case; the problem appears to remain an active research direction.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable points on manifolds
original_question: Using dynamics, can one estimate the Hausdorff dimension of v-approximable vectors lying in a nondegenerate submanifold of R^n?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $n\geq 2$ and a vector $v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n v_i = 1$. A point $x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $v$-approximable if there exist infinitely many $q\in\mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\max_{1\le i\le n}\|q x_i\|^{1/v_i} \;\le\; \frac{1}{q^{1+\varepsilon}}\qquad\text{for some }\varepsilon>0,$$
equivalently, if there are infinitely many $q\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ with $|q x_i - p_i|\le q^{-v_i(1+\varepsilon)/\text{(normalization)}}$, i.e. the inequalities $\|q x_i\|\le q^{-v_i}\psi(q)^{v_i}$ hold for infinitely many $q$ for some function $\psi(q)\to 0$. Let $W(v)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ denote the set of $v$-approximable vectors.

A smooth submanifold $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $d<n$ is called nondegenerate at a point $x\in M$ if, in some neighborhood of $x$, $M$ is parametrized by a $C^k$ map $f:U\to\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $U\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ open) such that the partial derivatives of $f$ at $f^{-1}(x)$ up to some order span $\mathbb{R}^n$. The manifold $M$ is nondegenerate if it is nondegenerate at almost every point.

Problem. Using methods from the dynamics of flows on the homogeneous space $\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Z})$ (in particular, quantitative nondivergence and the Dani correspondence relating Diophantine approximation to excursions of diagonal flows into the cusp), obtain estimates for the Hausdorff dimension
$$\dim_H\bigl(W(v)\cap M\bigr)$$
of the set of $v$-approximable vectors lying on a nondegenerate submanifold $M$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$.
status_search_result: There has been significant progress on computing the Hausdorff dimension of sets of (weighted) well/very-well approximable vectors lying on nondegenerate curves and manifolds, using quantitative nondivergence estimates for quasi-polynomial flows on homogeneous spaces (Beresnevich, Vaughan, Velani, Yang, Kleinbock, Margulis and others). Exact dimension formulas are known in various cases (curves, certain hypersurfaces), while sharp bounds in full generality for arbitrary nondegenerate manifolds and arbitrary weight vectors $v$ remain partially open.

original_question: Do there exist real numbers α and β such that for every ε>0, liminf_{q→∞} q(log q)^{2−ε}⟨qα⟩⟨qβ⟩ is positive?

$$\liminf_{q\to\infty}\, q\,(\log q)^{2-\varepsilon}\,\langle q\alpha\rangle\,\langle q\beta\rangle \;>\; 0,$$
where $q$ ranges over positive integers.

   liminf_{q→∞} q · ⟨qα⟩ · ⟨qβ⟩ = 0,
where q ranges over the positive integers.

context_brief: Finiteness of closed diagonal orbits in compact sets
original_question: For every compact set K in SL(3,R)/SL(3,Z), are there only finitely many closed A-orbits contained in K, where A is the full diagonal group in SL(3,R)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G = \mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$, let $\Gamma = \mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and consider the homogeneous space $X = G/\Gamma$ equipped with its standard locally compact topology. Let 
$$A = \{\mathrm{diag}(a_1,a_2,a_3) : a_i > 0,\ a_1 a_2 a_3 = 1\}$$
denote the full (positive) diagonal subgroup of $G$, acting on $X$ by left multiplication. A subset $Ax \subset X$ is called a closed $A$-orbit if it is closed in $X$.

Prove or disprove: for every compact subset $K \subset X$, the number of closed $A$-orbits $Ax$ contained in $K$ is finite.
status_search_result: This finiteness statement is a well-known conjecture of Margulis concerning closed orbits of the full diagonal group on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, closely connected to the Littlewood conjecture and to rigidity of higher-rank diagonal actions. Available literature (surveys by Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss, work of Eskin–Mozes, etc.) continues to treat it as an open problem; only partial results (e.g. measure-rigidity-based dimension bounds on exceptional sets, bounded-orbit results) are known.

context_brief: Finiteness in the Markov spectrum of decomposable forms
original_question: For every ε>0, is the set [ε,∞)∩{m(F)} finite, where m(F) is the normalized Markov minimum of a decomposable ternary form F?
self_contained_problem:
A ternary form $F:\mathbb{R}^3\to\mathbb{R}$ is called decomposable if it factors over $\mathbb{R}$ as a product of three real linear forms,
$$F(x_1,x_2,x_3)=L_1(x)\,L_2(x)\,L_3(x),\qquad L_i(x)=\sum_{j=1}^3 a_{ij}x_j,$$
and is assumed to be non-degenerate in the sense that $\det(a_{ij})\neq 0$. Define the (normalized) Markov minimum of such a form by
$$m(F)\;=\;\frac{\inf_{v\in\mathbb{Z}^3\setminus\{0\}}|F(v)|}{|\det(a_{ij})|}.$$
Note that $m(F)$ is invariant under the action of $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ on $F$ (by linear change of integral variables) and under nonzero real scaling of each linear factor. Let
$$\mathcal{M}\;=\;\{\,m(F)\,:\,F\text{ is a non-degenerate decomposable ternary form}\,\}\;\subset\;[0,\infty)$$
be the corresponding Markov spectrum. 

Prove or disprove: for every $\varepsilon>0$, the set $[\varepsilon,\infty)\cap\mathcal{M}$ is finite.
status_search_result: No source was found announcing a resolution of Margulis's question on finiteness of the part of the Markov spectrum of decomposable ternary forms above any positive threshold. Recent work on Margulis functions and quantitative Oppenheim-type problems addresses related questions about values of ternary forms but does not establish this finiteness statement. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: For a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form Q of dimension d≥3 that is not a multiple of a rational quadratic form, can one give an effective estimate T=T(ε) guaranteeing an integer vector x∈Z^d with 0<|Q(x)|<ε and ||x||<T?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be a nondegenerate indefinite quadratic form in $d \ge 3$ real variables, and assume $Q$ is not a scalar multiple of a quadratic form with rational coefficients. By the Oppenheim conjecture (now a theorem of Margulis), the set $Q(\mathbb{Z}^d)$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$; in particular, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $0<|Q(x)|<\varepsilon$.

Provide an effective bound $T=T(\varepsilon,Q)$, given by an explicit function of $\varepsilon$ (and of natural data attached to $Q$ such as its coefficients and a Diophantine measure of irrationality), such that one can guarantee the existence of $x\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ satisfying
$$0<|Q(x)|<\varepsilon \quad\text{and}\quad \|x\|<T(\varepsilon,Q).$$

Equivalently, find an effective rate at which the smallest nonzero integer vector $x$ with $|Q(x)|<\varepsilon$ may be required to grow as $\varepsilon\to 0^+$.
status_search_result: The problem of giving effective bounds in the Oppenheim conjecture has seen substantial recent progress. Lindenstrauss, Margulis, Mohammadi and Wang (and subsequent work with Yang) established effective versions of Oppenheim with polynomial error rates, in particular for indefinite ternary forms with algebraic coefficients and more generally via polynomial effective equidistribution of unipotent orbits. However, a fully general effective $T(\varepsilon)$ for all nondegenerate indefinite irrational forms in dimensions $d\ge 3$ with explicit dependence on the Diophantine properties of $Q$ is not yet completely settled, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

context_brief: Inhomogeneous minima of indefinite binary quadratic forms
original_question: For any nondegenerate indefinite binary quadratic form Q with rational coefficients that does not represent zero over Q, is the supremum m(Q) rational and isolated, and are both m(Q) and m2(Q) attained at points with coordinates in the splitting field of Q?
self_contained_problem:
Let $Q(x,y) = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ be a nondegenerate indefinite binary quadratic form with rational coefficients (so $a,b,c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$ is positive and not a rational square), and assume that $Q$ does not represent zero nontrivially over $\mathbb{Q}$ (equivalently, $Q(x,y)=0$ has no solution $(x,y) \in \mathbb{Q}^2 \setminus \{(0,0)\}$).

For a point $P = (x_0, y_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, define
$$M_Q(P) \;=\; \inf_{(p,q) \in \mathbb{Z}^2} \bigl| Q(x_0 + p,\, y_0 + q) \bigr|.$$
The function $M_Q$ is $\mathbb{Z}^2$-periodic. Let
$$m(Q) \;=\; \sup_{P \in \mathbb{R}^2} M_Q(P).$$
A point $P^*$ at which the supremum is attained is called an extremal point. Removing the orbit of all extremal points realising $m(Q)$ (under $\mathbb{Z}^2$-translation and the obvious symmetries), define the second inhomogeneous minimum
$$m_2(Q) \;=\; \sup\bigl\{ M_Q(P) : P \in \mathbb{R}^2,\ P \text{ not equivalent to any point realising } m(Q) \bigr\}.$$
We say $m(Q)$ is isolated if $m(Q) > m_2(Q)$. Let $K_Q$ denote the splitting field of $Q$, i.e. $K_Q = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac})$.

Prove or disprove: under the hypotheses on $Q$ above, the value $m(Q)$ is rational and isolated, and both $m(Q)$ and $m_2(Q)$ are attained at points whose coordinates lie in $K_Q$.

context_brief: Scars in Katok's Finsler metric example
original_question: In Katok's example of a Finsler metric on the two-dimensional sphere with ergodic geodesic flow and only two periodic orbits, do the closed geodesics correspond to scars?
self_contained_problem: Katok constructed a non-reversible Finsler metric on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ whose geodesic flow is ergodic (with respect to the Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle) and possesses exactly two prime closed geodesics. Consider the quantization of this geodesic flow: let $\{\psi_n\}$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions of the associated Laplace-type operator on $S^2$, with eigenvalues tending to infinity. A subsequence of eigenfunctions is said to exhibit a "scar" along an invariant set $K$ of the geodesic flow if the associated sequence of microlocal lift (Wigner) measures has a nonzero singular component supported on the lift of $K$ to the unit tangent bundle, contrary to the prediction of quantum ergodicity that almost all such measures equidistribute to the Liouville measure. Question: in Katok's example, do the two closed geodesics support scars, i.e., is there a positive-density (or any) subsequence of high-energy eigenfunctions whose semiclassical limit measures have a nonzero singular component concentrated on the lift of one of these two closed geodesics?
status_search_result: The geometric and dynamical properties of Katok's Finsler example on $S^2$ are well studied, including the optimality result of Bangert–Long on the minimum number of closed geodesics. However, no source located addresses the specific quantum-mechanical question of whether the two closed geodesics in Katok's example support scars in the spectral/semiclassical sense; the status of this question appears unresolved.

original_question: If X has negative sectional curvature and μ_i are the probability measures |φ_i(x)|^2 dV(x) associated with Laplace eigenfunctions, does μ_i converge to dV as i→∞?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a closed (compact, boundary-less) smooth Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, with Riemannian volume measure $dV$ normalized so that $\int_X dV = 1$. Let $\Delta$ denote the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, and let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X, dV)$ consisting of eigenfunctions $\Delta \varphi_i = \lambda_i \varphi_i$ with eigenvalues $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le \cdots \to \infty$. $$\int_X f(x)\,|\varphi_i(x)|^2\,dV(x) \;\longrightarrow\; \int_X f(x)\,dV(x) \qquad (i\to\infty).$$
status_search_result: The Rudnick–Sarnak quantum unique ergodicity conjecture for general compact negatively curved manifolds remains open. original_question: For an arithmetic manifold with joint eigenfunctions of invariant differential operators and Hecke operators, is Riemannian volume the only arithmetic quantum limit?

original_question: Let X=Γ\H^2 with Γ a noncocompact arithmetic lattice. For all compactly supported continuous functions f and g on X, does the ratio of their μ_i-integrals converge to the corresponding ratio of their Riemannian-volume integrals as i→∞?

Let $\mathbb{H}^2$ denote the hyperbolic plane, and let $\Gamma \subset \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a noncocompact arithmetic lattice. $$\frac{\int_X f\, d\mu_i}{\int_X g\, d\mu_i} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{\int_X f\, dV}{\int_X g\, dV} \qquad \text{as } i \to \infty.$$

original_question: For generic negatively curved compact Riemannian manifolds, do Laplace eigenfunctions φ_i have Gaussian value distribution, so that Vol({x∈X:a≤φ_i(x)≤b}) converges to (1/√(2π))∫_a^b exp(−t^2/2)dt as i→∞?

Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold without boundary, normalized to have total volume $1$, and assume that $X$ has negative sectional curvature (so its geodesic flow is Anosov). Let $\Delta$ denote the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, and let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of real-valued eigenfunctions, $\Delta \varphi_i = \lambda_i \varphi_i$, with $0 = \lambda_0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \to \infty$, and normalized so that $\int_X \varphi_i^2\, d\mathrm{vol} = 1$.

$$\mathrm{Vol}\bigl(\{x \in X : a \le \varphi_i(x) \le b\}\bigr) \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_a^b e^{-t^2/2}\, dt \qquad \text{as } i \to \infty.$$

original_question: For generic negatively curved compact Riemannian manifolds X and a∈C_c^∞(S^*X,R) with Liouville mean zero, does ξ_i(a)=λ_i^{1/4}|⟨Op(a)φ_i,φ_i⟩| have a Gaussian limiting distribution with variance V(a)=∫_{−∞}^{∞}∫_{S^*X}a(xg^t)a(x)dλ(x)dt, including convergence of second moments and interval counts as stated?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, and let $S^*X$ denote its unit cotangent bundle, equipped with the geodesic flow $\{g^t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ and the normalized Liouville measure $\lambda$. Let $\Delta$ be the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $X$, and let $\{\varphi_i\}_{i\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(X)$ consisting of eigenfunctions of $\Delta$ with eigenvalues $0\le \lambda_1\le \lambda_2\le \cdots$. Assume $a\in C_c^\infty(S^*X,\mathbb R)$ satisfies $\int_{S^*X} a\,d\lambda = 0$, and set
$$\xi_i(a) := \lambda_i^{1/4}\,\bigl|\langle \mathrm{Op}(a)\varphi_i,\varphi_i\rangle\bigr|,\qquad V(a) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\!\int_{S^*X} a(x g^t)\,a(x)\,d\lambda(x)\,dt.$$

For a "generic" such manifold $X$, prove or disprove the following two statements as $\lambda\to\infty$:

(1) (Convergence of second moments) 
$$\frac{1}{N(\lambda)}\sum_{\lambda_i\le \lambda}\xi_i(a)^2 \longrightarrow V(a),$$
where $N(\lambda) = \#\{i:\lambda_i\le\lambda\}$.

(2) (Gaussian limit law) For every interval $I\subset\mathbb R$,
$$\frac{1}{N(\lambda)}\,\#\bigl\{i:\lambda_i\le \lambda,\ V(a)^{-1/2}\xi_i(a)\in I\bigr\} \longrightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_I e^{-t^2/2}\,dt.$$

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
original_question: Do periodic orbits in a triangular billiard correspond to scars; more precisely, are there quantum limits supported on periodic orbits?
self_contained_problem:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a triangle, and consider the billiard flow on $T$ (the geodesic flow on $T$ with elastic reflections from the boundary). Consider the associated quantum problem: let $\{\phi_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be an orthonormal basis of $L^2(T)$ consisting of Dirichlet (or Neumann) eigenfunctions of the Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $T$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_n \to \infty$. To each $\phi_n$ one associates a microlocal lift $\mu_n$, a positive measure on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*T$ whose projection to $T$ has density $|\phi_n|^2$. A quantum limit is any weak-$*$ accumulation point of the sequence $\{\mu_n\}$; every quantum limit is invariant under the billiard flow.

A quantum limit $\mu$ is said to be supported on a periodic orbit $\gamma$ of the billiard flow if $\mathrm{supp}(\mu) \subset \gamma$. The problem is the following: does there exist a triangle $T$ and a periodic orbit $\gamma$ of its billiard flow such that some quantum limit of Laplace eigenfunctions on $T$ is supported on $\gamma$? In other words, do periodic orbits in triangular billiards correspond to scars in the sense of giving rise to quantum limits concentrated on them?
status_search_result: No mathematical proof has been found establishing or ruling out the existence of quantum limits supported on periodic orbits in triangular billiards. Numerical and physical studies (e.g., on quantum chaos in triangular billiards) report strong scarring effects associated with short periodic orbits and bouncing-ball modes, but these are empirical observations rather than a rigorous classification of quantum limits. The problem appears to remain open.

original_question: Can one classify all quantum limits of eigenfunctions of a polygonal billiard?
self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (a compact, simply connected planar domain whose boundary is a finite union of straight line segments). Consider the Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ on $P$, which has a discrete spectrum $0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \to \infty$ with a corresponding orthonormal basis of real eigenfunctions $\{\varphi_n\}_{n \ge 1} \subset L^2(P)$ satisfying $-\Delta \varphi_n = \lambda_n \varphi_n$ and $\varphi_n|_{\partial P} = 0$. To each eigenfunction $\varphi_n$ associate the probability measure $\mu_n$ on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*P$ defined via its microlocal lift (so that the projection of $\mu_n$ to $P$ has density $|\varphi_n|^2$). A quantum limit of the billiard $P$ is any weak-$*$ accumulation point of the sequence $(\mu_n)_{n \ge 1}$ as $n \to \infty$; equivalently, it is a probability measure on $S^*P$ that is invariant under the billiard geodesic flow and arises as such a limit along some subsequence $\varphi_{n_k}$.

Problem: For an arbitrary polygon $P$, classify all probability measures on $S^*P$ that can occur as quantum limits of Dirichlet eigenfunctions of $P$.
status_search_result: The classification of quantum limits for polygonal (in particular rational and irrational) billiards remains open. Partial results exist (e.g., quantum ergodicity for certain rational polygons, scarring phenomena, results by Hassell–Hillairet on ergodic billiards that are not quantum unique ergodic), but a full classification of quantum limits for general polygonal billiards is not established.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
context_brief: Equidistribution of generic special-point Galois orbits
original_question: Let {x_n} be a sequence of special points on a Shimura variety, and suppose x_n lies outside any special subvariety for sufficiently large n. Do the Galois orbits of x_n become equidistributed as n→∞ with respect to normalized Haar measure?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a Shimura variety associated with a Shimura datum $(G,X)$, defined over its reflex field $E$. Recall that a point $x \in S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ is called a special point if it corresponds to a CM point, i.e., it is the image of a point $h \in X$ whose Mumford–Tate group is a torus. A special subvariety of $S$ is an irreducible component of the image of a Shimura sub-datum morphism; in particular special subvarieties contain a dense set of special points. The Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/E)$ acts on the (finite) set of special points of any given type, and for each special point $x$ one obtains a finite Galois orbit $O(x) \subset S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \subset S(\mathbb{C})$. Let $\mu_S$ denote the canonical probability measure on $S(\mathbb{C})$ induced by the normalized Haar measure on the relevant arithmetic quotient.

For a finite subset $F \subset S(\mathbb{C})$ write $\mu_F := \frac{1}{|F|}\sum_{y\in F}\delta_y$ for the normalized counting measure.

Question: Let $\{x_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of special points of $S$ such that, for every proper special subvariety $Z \subsetneq S$, one has $x_n \notin Z$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Is it true that the normalized counting measures $\mu_{O(x_n)}$ on the Galois orbits converge weakly to $\mu_S$ as $n \to \infty$?
status_search_result: The conjecture (an equidistribution statement closely tied to the André–Oort conjecture) has been established in many cases. Work of Clozel–Ullmo, Ullmo–Yafaev, and others proves equidistribution conditional on lower bounds for the size of Galois orbits (which follow from GRH or, for $\mathcal{A}_g$, from Tsimerman's unconditional bounds). Tsimerman's proof of André–Oort for $\mathcal{A}_g$ and the subsequent unconditional proof of André–Oort by Pila–Shankar–Tsimerman provide the necessary Galois-orbit lower bounds in those settings, yielding the equidistribution unconditionally for $\mathcal{A}_g$ and several mixed Shimura cases, but in full generality the statement still depends on Galois-orbit lower bounds that are not unconditionally known.

paper_title: OPEN PROBLEMS IN DYNAMICS AND RELATED FIELDS
original_question: Can one give an ergodic-theoretic proof of the equidistribution of special points on SL_2(Z)\H^2?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^2 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im}(z) > 0\}$ denote the upper half-plane, equipped with the action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ by Möbius transformations. The modular surface is $X = \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})  ackslash \mathbb{H}^2$, endowed with the (normalized) hyperbolic probability measure $\mu$ coming from $ rac{dx\,dy}{y^2}$.

A point $z \in \mathbb{H}^2$ is called a CM point (special point) of discriminant $D < 0$ if $z$ satisfies a primitive integral quadratic equation $a z^2 + b z + c = 0$ with $a > 0$, $\gcd(a,b,c) = 1$, and $b^2 - 4ac = D$. For each negative fundamental discriminant $D$, the set $\Lambda_D \subset X$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-equivalence classes of CM points of discriminant $D$ is finite, of cardinality equal to the class number $h(D)$.

It is a classical theorem (Duke) that as $D 	o -\infty$ through fundamental discriminants, the uniform probability measures $\mu_D =  rac{1}{h(D)} \sum_{z \in \Lambda_D} \delta_z$ converge weakly to $\mu$.

Problem: Give a proof of this equidistribution statement using only methods of ergodic theory and homogeneous dynamics (for instance via entropy methods, measure rigidity, or unipotent/torus dynamics on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})  ackslash \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ or related homogeneous spaces), without invoking subconvexity bounds for $L$-functions or harmonic analysis on automorphic forms.
status_search_result: An ergodic-theoretic approach to Duke's equidistribution theorem for closed geodesics and CM points on the modular surface was developed by Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel, and Venkatesh, using entropy methods and measure rigidity for torus actions, refining Linnik's ergodic method. Their results give an ergodic proof under an auxiliary splitting condition (e.g., a fixed split prime), so the problem is largely solved in the conditional/Linnik-type sense but a fully unconditional ergodic proof matching Duke's full theorem is not yet available.

paper_title: THE HODGE CONJECTURE
context_brief: Integral Hodge classes and Atiyah–Hirzebruch differentials
original_question: Let X be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and let c be an integral cohomology class in H^{2p}(X, Z) of Hodge type (p,p) that survives all differentials d_r in the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence from cohomology to topological K-theory. Must every such class c be an integral linear combination of cohomology classes cl(Z) of algebraic cycles Z of codimension p on X?
self_contained_problem:
Let X be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety. Consider the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence
  E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X, K^q(pt)) ⇒ K^{p+q}(X)
from singular cohomology to topological K-theory, with its successive differentials d_r (r ≥ 2). For each codimension-p algebraic cycle Z on X, the cohomology class cl(Z) ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) is of Hodge type (p,p) and is annihilated by all differentials d_r of this spectral sequence.

Question: Let c ∈ H^{2p}(X, Z) be an integral cohomology class whose image in H^{2p}(X, C) lies in the (p,p)-component of the Hodge decomposition, and which is killed by every differential d_r of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence. Must c be expressible as a Z-linear combination
  c = Σ n_i · cl(Z_i)
of classes of codimension-p algebraic subvarieties Z_i of X?
status_search_result: The statement is a well-known refinement of the integral Hodge conjecture due to Atiyah–Hirzebruch and revisited by Totaro. While the integral Hodge conjecture itself has many counterexamples (Atiyah–Hirzebruch torsion classes, Kollár hypersurfaces, Benoist–Ottem Enriques threefolds, etc.), all known counterexamples are obstructed precisely by some Atiyah–Hirzebruch (or cobordism) differential. No counterexample is known to the refined statement that integral (p,p) classes lying in the kernel of every d_r are algebraic, and standard references (nLab, surveys on the Hodge conjecture, Totaro's work) record this as an open problem.

paper_title: THE HODGE CONJECTURE
original_question: Among integral (p,p)-classes on a smooth projective complex algebraic variety that are known or conjectured to come from algebraic cycles, which classes should be effective in the strong sense of being the class cl(Z) of a single codimension-p algebraic cycle Z, rather than only a difference of such classes?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and let $p$ be an integer with $0 \le p \le \dim X$. The singular cohomology $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ maps to $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$, which carries the Hodge decomposition $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{r+s=2p} H^{r,s}(X)$. An integral $(p,p)$-class is an element of
\[ \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z}) := \{\alpha \in H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z}) : \alpha_{\mathbb{C}} \in H^{p,p}(X)\}. \]
A codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle on $X$ is a finite formal $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$-linear combination $Z = \sum_i n_i Z_i$ of closed irreducible subvarieties $Z_i \subset X$ of codimension $p$ (with non-negative integer coefficients $n_i \ge 0$); its cohomology class $\mathrm{cl}(Z) \in H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ lies in $\mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$. Call a class $\alpha \in \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ effective if $\alpha = \mathrm{cl}(Z)$ for some such (non-negative) codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle $Z$, as opposed to a difference $\mathrm{cl}(Z_1) - \mathrm{cl}(Z_2)$ of two such classes.

Problem: Characterize, intrinsically in terms of Hodge-theoretic or cohomological data, the subset of effective classes inside the cone of those integral $(p,p)$-classes on $X$ that arise as integral linear combinations of classes of codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles. In particular, give a necessary and sufficient criterion to decide, for a given $\alpha \in \mathrm{Hdg}^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ that is known to be an integral combination of algebraic cycle classes, whether $\alpha$ is effective in the strong sense $\alpha = \mathrm{cl}(Z)$ for a single (non-negative) codimension-$p$ cycle $Z$.
status_search_result: The question of which integral (p,p)-classes are effective in the strong sense of being represented by a single codimension-p algebraic cycle (rather than a difference of such cycles) is widely regarded as open. Standard expository sources on the Hodge conjecture and surveys of known cases discuss only representability as rational/integral combinations, and explicitly note that no intrinsic criterion is known for distinguishing effective classes from differences of effective classes.

paper_title: THE HODGE CONJECTURE
context_brief: Algebraic cycles inside the intermediate Jacobian
original_question: For a smooth projective complex algebraic variety X and a fixed codimension p, let J^p(X) be the extension of the group of integral cohomology classes of type (p,p) by the intermediate Jacobian J^p(X)^0, and let A^p(X) be the subgroup of J^p(X) generated by codimension-p algebraic cycles on X. What subgroup of J^p(X) is A^p(X)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex algebraic variety, and fix an integer $p$ with $0 \le p \le \dim X$. Consider the singular cohomology group $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ and its image in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$, which has a Hodge decomposition $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C}) = \bigoplus_{r+s=2p} H^{r,s}(X)$. Let $\mathrm{Hg}^p(X) \subset H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ denote the group of integral classes whose image in $H^{2p}(X,\mathbb{C})$ lies in $H^{p,p}(X)$ (the Hodge classes of codimension $p$). Define the intermediate Jacobian
$$J^p(X)^0 = \frac{H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{C})}{F^p H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{C}) + H^{2p-1}(X,\mathbb{Z})},$$
where $F^p$ denotes the Hodge filtration. Let $J^p(X)$ be the complex Lie group fitting in the extension
$$0 \longrightarrow J^p(X)^0 \longrightarrow J^p(X) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Hg}^p(X) \longrightarrow 0.$$
A codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle on $X$ that is homologous to zero has an Abel–Jacobi image in $J^p(X)^0$, and an arbitrary codimension-$p$ algebraic cycle has a class in $J^p(X)$ lifting its cohomology class. Let $A^p(X) \subseteq J^p(X)$ be the subgroup generated by the classes of all codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles on $X$.

Problem: Give an intrinsic description (in Hodge-theoretic or geometric terms) of the subgroup $A^p(X)$ inside $J^p(X)$. Equivalently, characterize which elements of $J^p(X)$ are represented by $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of codimension-$p$ algebraic cycles on $X$.
status_search_result: The problem of describing $A^p(X)$ inside $J^p(X)$ is widely regarded as open: Griffiths' work, and later results of Clemens, Voisin and others, show the image of the Abel–Jacobi map can contain transcendental and non-finitely-generated parts, and no conjecture is known to characterize it in general.

paper_title: THE HODGE CONJECTURE
context_brief: Algorithmic detection of Hodge classes in families
original_question: Consider a smooth projective algebraic family f : X → S defined over the algebraic closure Q̄ of Q in C, and fix an integral cohomology class on a typical fiber X_0. Is there an algorithm that decides whether this class becomes of Hodge type (p,p) on some fiber somewhere over the parameter space S?
self_contained_problem:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a smooth projective morphism of algebraic varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, the algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}$ in $\mathbb{C}$, so that $(X_s)_{s\in S}$ is an algebraic family of smooth projective varieties. Fix a base point $0 \in S(\mathbb{C})$ and an integral cohomology class $\alpha \in H^{2p}(X_0, \mathbb{Z})$. For each $s \in S(\mathbb{C})$, the singular cohomology $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{C})$ carries the Hodge decomposition $\bigoplus_{i+j=2p} H^{i,j}(X_s)$; one says that a class in $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{Z})$ is of type $(p,p)$ at $s$ if its image in $H^{2p}(X_s, \mathbb{C})$ lies in $H^{p,p}(X_s)$. Using parallel transport via the Gauss–Manin connection along paths in $S$, the class $\alpha$ determines a (multi-valued) section of the local system $R^{2p}f_*\mathbb{Z}$, and at each $s \in S$ we may ask whether some parallel transport of $\alpha$ to $X_s$ is of type $(p,p)$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given such data $(f : X \to S, \alpha)$ specified over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, decides whether there exists $s \in S(\mathbb{C})$ at which (some parallel transport of) $\alpha$ becomes a class of type $(p,p)$ on $X_s$?
status_search_result: No algorithm is known to decide whether a given integral cohomology class of a typical fiber in a smooth projective family over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ becomes of Hodge type $(p,p)$ somewhere over the base. The problem is generally regarded as open; while there has been work on computer-assisted exploration of Hodge classes, no decision procedure has been established, and the underlying Hodge conjecture remains an open Millennium Prize Problem.
